title: Preclinical evidence for mifepristone in breast cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis of animal studies.
abstract: Mifepristone (MIF), an antagonist of the progesterone receptor (PR) and glucocorticoid receptor (GR), has shown antitumor activity in experimental breast cancer, but the consistency and certainty of the preclinical evidence remain unclear. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure through May 5, 2026, for animal studies evaluating MIF alone or in combination with other anticancer treatments. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using Hedges' g with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and the Knapp-Hartung adjustment. Seventeen studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis. MIF monotherapy was associated with lower tumor volume (Hedges' g = -2.77, 95% confidence interval [CI] -4.07 to -1.47) and tumor weight (Hedges' g = -2.52, 95% CI -4.74 to -0.29), whereas the overall tumor-area estimate was inconclusive (Hedges' g = -0.80, 95% CI -1.77 to 0.16). MIF-containing combination regimens were associated with lower tumor volume than the corresponding MIF-free backbone regimens (Hedges' g = -1.28, 95% CI -1.94 to -0.63). No statistically significant difference in terminal body weight was observed under either treatment framework. Exploratory subgroup analysis identified an interaction between PR isoform context and the tumor-area effect estimate (P for interaction = 0.0004), whereas no evidence of an interaction was observed between the broader breast-cancer biological contexts for tumor volume (P for interaction = 0.769). Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes, and the certainty of evidence was low to very low. The available animal evidence supports further investigation of MIF in biologically characterized breast cancer models, but does not establish clinical efficacy, validated predictors of treatment response, or overall treatment safety. PROSPERO: CRD420261386224.

title: Remimazolam ED95 for Preoperative Sedation in Children with Obstructive Sleep Apnea, with Obesity or a Reference-Range BMI: A Biased-Coin Dose-Finding Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity may alter total-body-weight dosing of remimazolam, whereas obstructive sleep apnea narrows the respiratory safety margin. We estimated the ED95 for protocol-defined preoperative sedation in children with obesity or a reference-range body mass index (BMI).
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center sequential dose-finding study, 80 children aged 3-17 years with a clinical OSA diagnosis undergoing adenoidectomy and/or tonsillectomy entered study-defined obesity (BMI-for-age >95th percentile) or reference-BMI (25th-84th percentile) groups (40 each). Independent biased-coin sequences used total-body-weight doses, starting at 0.20 mg/kg with 0.05 mg/kg steps. The response was a Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) score ≥4 at 3 minutes after completion of a 1-minute intravenous bolus. Isotonic regression and 2000 bootstrap resamples yielded ED95 estimates and bias-corrected percentile 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Responses occurred in 35/40 (87.5%) participants in the obesity group and 34/40 (85.0%) in the reference-BMI group. ED95 estimates were 0.38 mg/kg (95% CI, 0.32-0.39) and 0.44 mg/kg (95% CI, 0.39-0.44), respectively. The difference was -0.05 mg/kg (95% CI, -0.13 to 0.05). During 15-minute observation, one child per group developed hypoxemia (SpO2 93%) that resolved after a jaw-thrust maneuver. One reference-BMI participant developed bradycardia (50 beats/min), which responded to atropine. No child had a ≥30% decrease in mean arterial pressure.
CONCLUSION: The protocol-specific ED95 values of a 1-min remimazolam bolus for RSS ≥4 at 3 min were 0.38 mg/kg in children with obesity and 0.44 mg/kg in children with a reference-range BMI.

title: Testing peripheral and central therapies for provoked vestibulodynia: results from the UPDATe trial.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vestibulodynia (VBD) is a common chronic pelvic pain condition with heterogeneous clinical presentation, including subtypes distinguished by the presence (VBD-central; VBD-c) or absence (VBD-peripheral; VBD-p) of comorbid pain conditions. Despite frequent prescribing of topical therapies such as lidocaine/estradiol and centrally-acting agents such as tricyclic antidepressants, high-quality evidence for efficacy, alone or in combination, remains limited. This study evaluated effects of peripheral, central, and combined pharmacologic treatments for two VBD subtypes and whether treatment response varied by subtype.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03844412) at two academic medical centers. Women aged 18-50 with clinician-confirmed VBD were randomized to one of four treatment arms: 1) topical 5% lidocaine + 0.05% estradiol vaginal cream and placebo pill, 2) oral nortriptyline pill and placebo cream, 3) combined active pill and cream, or 4) double placebo for 16 weeks. The primary outcome was provoked vulvovaginal pain by a standardized tampon test (0-10 numeric rating scale).
RESULTS: Of 209 participants, 69 had VBD-p and 140 had VBD-c. Tampon test pain decreased modestly across all arms, with the greatest proportion of decrease in the combined nortriptyline plus lidocaine/estradiol group, but there was no difference between subtypes. In the primary model, baseline pain strongly predicted Week 16 pain (β = 0.68, p < 0.001), and while many participants had a decrease in pain over time, no treatment produced a statistically significant reduction compared with placebo.
CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, neither peripheral nor centrally targeted pharmacotherapies demonstrated superiority over placebo in reducing provoked vulvovaginal pain at 16 weeks.

title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis.
METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.
RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status.
CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

title: Body Mass Index, Valsartan, and Myocardial Remodeling in Early-Stage Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Secondary Analysis of the Randomized VANISH Trial.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with adverse outcomes in overt hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the prevalence and impact of elevated body mass index (BMI) in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is uncertain.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the randomized VANISH (Valsartan for Attenuating Disease Evolution in Early Sarcomeric Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy) trial, participants were categorized according to baseline BMI (nonelevated or elevated [≥85th percentile if age <18 years; ≥25 kg/m2 if age ≥18 years]). Exercise capacity (peak oxygen uptake [milliliters per kilogram per minute]) and cardiac imaging parameters were evaluated by baseline BMI and 2-year change in BMI.
RESULTS: Among 171 (96%) participants (mean age, 23±10 years; 39% female sex; 97% White), 82 (48%) had nonelevated BMI and 89 (52%) had an elevated BMI. After covariate adjustment, higher baseline BMI was associated with lower peak oxygen uptake; lower left ventricular systolic and diastolic function; higher left ventricular mass; and higher atrial, ventricular, and extracellular volumes. Similarly, greater 2-year increases in BMI were associated with greater declines in peak oxygen uptake and greater increases in left ventricular mass. Participants with elevated BMI were more likely to develop late gadolinium enhancement over 2 years (adjusted odds ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-11.9]; P=0.033). Valsartan appeared to modestly attenuate 2-year increases in body weight versus placebo (adjusted mean difference, -3.1% [95% CI, -6.2 to -0.1%]; P=0.042). Baseline BMI did not appear to modify the effect of valsartan on cardiac remodeling (Pinteraction=0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated BMI was common and associated with greater hypertrophic, eccentric, and fibrotic remodeling in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Two-year increases in BMI were associated with greater phenotypic progression. These findings suggest prevention and treatment of elevated BMI may attenuate hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression.

title: Effects of evolocumab on lipid profile and circulating endothelial biomarkers in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of early evolocumab plus atorvastatin on lipid metabolism, circulating endothelial biomarkers, and inflammation in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI).MethodsIn this single-center, open-label trial, 90 patients were randomized 1:1 to atorvastatin 20 mg/day (control, n=45) or atorvastatin 20 mg/day plus evolocumab 140 mg biweekly (combination, n=45) for 12 weeks. One patient withdrew from the combination group at day 28; last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) was applied to impute missing 12-week endpoints for the withdrawn participant. All 90 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) analytic population. Lipid profiles, endothelial biomarkers, inflammatory cytokines, and safety outcomes were assessed at baseline and 12 weeks. Standard Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) with 12-week value as dependent variable and corresponding baseline level as covariate was used to compare between-group treatment effects for normally distributed outcomes; non-parametric tests were applied for non-normally distributed data. All secondary biomarker, cardiac function and safety analyses were predefined as exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.ResultsBaseline characteristics were well-balanced. The primary endpoint-change in LDL-C from baseline-was significantly greater in the combination group (adjusted mean difference: -0.31 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.60 to -0.02, P=0.037). A significantly higher proportion achieved the guideline-recommended LDL-C target of <1.4 mmol/L (48.89% vs. 22.2%, P=0.007). Secondary endpoints showed favorable changes in nitric oxide, endothelin-1, and sICAM-1 (all P<0.05), and a significant reduction in IL-6 by non-parametric testing (P=0.005). No significant between-group differences were observed for other biomarkers, cardiac function indices, or adverse events (all P>0.05).ConclusionsIn this small, single-center trial, early evolocumab added to moderate-intensity atorvastatin was associated with additional LDL-C reduction and favorable changes in selected circulating endothelial biomarkers and IL-6 over 12 weeks in STEMI patients post-PPCI, no major safety signal was observed in this short-term study. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials using guideline-directed high-intensity statin therapy as the standard of care. Chinese Clinical Trial Register submission ID: PID343553 (application currently under administrative review, not publicly released).

title: Bridging evidence gaps in opioid-sparing postoperative pain control for percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a network meta-analysis identifying optimal strategies.
abstract: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is the gold standard for large renal calculi, yet postoperative pain from tract dilation, capsule injury, and inflammation often delays recovery, prolongs hospital stays, and reduces patient satisfaction. Amid the opioid crisis, reliance on opioids for pain control raises concerns over adverse effects like respiratory depression, nausea, and dependence. This has spurred interest in opioid-sparing multimodal strategies, with recent studies suggesting feasibility of opioid-free discharge and comparable relief from NSAIDs with fewer side effects. However, robust comparative evidence remains scarce. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluates and ranks postoperative analgesic strategies in PCNL, aiming to highlight approaches that may reduce opioid use while improving clinical outcomes in endourology. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library up to March 11, 2025 for RCTs assessing VAS pain in adults undergoing PCNL. Interventions grouped: local anesthesia/nerve blocks, intravenous analgesics, local instillation, intrathecal anesthesia, aromatherapy. Bayesian NMA used ADDIS v1.16.8/R v4.0.5, with MCMC simulations, node-splitting for consistency, SMAA for benefit-risk of VAS (<24h, ≥24h) and complications. 45 RCTs (2,626 patients) formed consistent network without significant inconsistency/heterogeneity. Levobupivacaine outperformed bupivacaine/ropivacaine in VAS reduction (<24h, ≥24h) via erector spinae plane block/local infiltration. Non-opioid analgesics (NSAIDs/paracetamol) showed superior efficacy; opioids excelled short-term but not long-term. IV paracetamol plus LI-levobupivacaine ranked highest in the multicriteria analysis, although the benefit-risk ranking should be interpreted cautiously because the safety component was based on sparse and imprecise data. Limitations: RCT protocol variability (e.g., pain assessment), moderate bias in 21 studies, limited data for high-risk subgroups (e.g., renal impairment, obesity). Comparative safety could not be established because complication data were sparse and estimates were highly imprecise. This NMA supports levobupivacaine and NSAID-based IV analgesics for PCNL pain management, positioning IV-Paracetamol+LI-Levobupivacaine as a leading opioid-sparing multimodal option to address complex pain profiles. These findings encourage safer practices amid opioid concerns, potentially accelerating recovery, shortening stays, and enhancing endourology patient outcomes.Trial registration: PROSPERO CRD42024600872.

title: Effect of injectable platelet rich fibrin augmented with vitamin c compared to injectable platelet rich fibrin alone on healing of necrotic mature single rooted teeth with chronic periapical periodontitis following regenerative endodontic therapy (a randomized controlled trial).
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the healing potential, postoperative pain and clinical normalcy associated with injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C in regenerative endodontic procedure using cone-beam computed tomography and two-dimensional radiograph.
METHODS: Twenty-eight healthy patients with mature permanent single-rooted teeth diagnosed with pulp necrosis and chronic apical periodontitis were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 14). Regenerative endodontic treatment was performed using injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C (intervention group) and injectable platelet-rich fibrin alone (control group). Periapical healing was assessed using CBCT and periapical radiographs over 12 months. Postoperative pain and clinical normalcy were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Both groups showed significant lesion reduction at 12 months (P = 0.001), with no significant between-group differences in postoperative lesion size (P = 0.981) or reduction magnitude (P = 0.497). CBCT-PAI scores improved in both groups without significant intergroup differences at baseline or follow-up. Two-dimensional radiographs showed a baseline difference (P = 0.007) but no postoperative differences; both groups demonstrated significant longitudinal reduction (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain scores were comparable between groups at all time points (P > 0.05), with a significant temporal decrease observed only in the intervention group (P = 0.001). All teeth remained asymptomatic during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Both i-PRF combined with vitamin C and i-PRF alone appear to be effective regenerative scaffolds, demonstrating comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes in regenerative endodontic procedures.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT05585359), registered on 14 October 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05585359 .

title: Comparative efficacy of topical garlic extract and 20% podophyllin solution in the treatment of female genital warts: a triple-blind randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genital warts caused by human papillomavirus are common sexually transmitted infections, with no single therapy providing consistent clearance. Garlic extract has antiviral and antiproliferative properties and may offer a low-cost treatment.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of topical 5% garlic extract with 20% podophyllin solution in women with genital warts.
METHODS: Seventy-four women were randomized to 5% garlic extract (n = 37) or 20% podophyllin (n = 37), applied weekly for four weeks. Wart size and count were assessed using marginal models (generalized estimating equations). The primary outcome was change in mean wart size and the secondary outcome was change in wart count.
RESULTS: Mean wart size decreased from 1.61 ± 0.81 to 0.60 ± 0.82 mm with garlic extract and from 2.96 ± 7.99 to 0.62 ± 0.73 mm with podophyllin. The between-group p-value at final assessment was 0.756; group × time interaction p values were 0.329 for wart size and 0.583 for count. Among 35 and 37 participants analyzed, complete response occurred in 18 (51.4%) and 19 (51.4%), respectively; complete or partial response occurred in 23 (65.7%) and 25 (67.6%). Itching and burning occurred in 8 (21.6%) garlic-treated participants each.
CONCLUSION: Both treatments reduced wart size and count, with similar response rates. Four-week follow-up precluded assessment of durability and recurrence.

title: Biologic treatments for palmoplantar psoriasis and palmoplantar pustulosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: The treatment of palmoplantar psoriasis (PPP), manifesting as hyperkeratotic plaques or pustular lesions (palmoplantar pustulosis -PPPP), is challenging. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy of various biologic treatments for PPP through a network meta-analysis. Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving biologic treatments for adult patients with PPP or PPPP. Databases searched included PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, and trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP). The search was conducted from inception to May 2026. Studies comparing biologic agents were included. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving ppPASI75 or equivalent PGA 0/1 at week 14-16. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was performed, reporting 95% credible intervals (CrI). 20 RCTs with 2,158 patients were included. Significant efficacy was observed for adalimumab (OR: 6.8, 95% CrI: 1.5-31), guselkumab 100 mg (OR: 7.4, 95% CrI: 2.0-2), ixekizumab (OR: 10.0, 95% CrI: 2.2-44), and secukinumab (OR: 6.1, 95% CrI: 1.7-27) compared to placebo. SUCRA values were highest for ixekizumab (87.2%), guselkumab 100 mg (84.1%), adalimumab (76.5%), and secukinumab (71.3%). Patients with exclusive palmoplantar involvement had a more challenging response to treatment. Biologic therapies offer significant improvement in managing PPP and PPPP. Specific biologic agents showed superior efficacy, allowing optimization of treatment strategies; however, these findings are based on indirect comparisons and heterogeneous populations, and should therefore be interpreted with caution. Future research should focus on direct comparisons, phenotype-specific trials, and long-term efficacy to enhance patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: Impact of different protein sources on acute muscle protein synthesis following resistance training: a systematic review with standard and dose-response network meta-analyses.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of protein intake and resistance training (RT) plays a pivotal role in stimulating muscle protein synthesis (MPS), yet the impact of different protein sources remains an area of active investigation. Therefore, a systematic review incorporating standard and dose‒response network meta-analyses was performed.
METHODS: Systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, EBSCOhost (including MEDLINE, SPORTDiscus, CINAHL), and Scopus. Eligible studies included healthy adults (≥18 years) who were undergoing acute resistance exercise followed by a single protein bolus (any type or dose, except blends or enriched with anabolic agents). Muscle biopsies were required before and after RT/protein intake without additional food in between. Trials measuring hourly MPS rates via tracer techniques were included (n = 51).
RESULTS: In the standard network meta-analysis (NMA), native whey (P-score = 0.81, MD = 0.05% [0.00; 0.10]), pea protein (0.77, MD = 0.05% [-0.02; 0.11]), whole egg protein (0.72, MD = 0.04% [-0.01; 0.09]), mycoprotein (0.66, MD = 0.03% [-0.02; 0.08]), and whey protein (0.58, MD = 0.02% [0.01; 0.04]) ranked highest for estimated efficacy in stimulating post-RT hourly MPS (in descending order) (only whey protein showed a statistically significant effect) with low to moderate certainty of evidence. Dose‒response NMA revealed that certain animal- (native whey and whole egg protein) and plant- (pea and mycoprotein) based protein sources to show the highest predicted MPS responses with doses of 18-25 g.
CONCLUSIONS: Animal- (native whey, whey, whole egg) and plant-based (pea, mycoprotein) proteins ranked similarly for estimated acute MPS stimulation when combined with RT; however, only whey protein showed a statistically significant effect, and protein sources represented by few studies should be interpreted with caution.

title: Digital health technologies for the prevention and management of urinary tract infections in menopausal women: A systematic review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary tract infections are among the most common infectious diseases in women, with incidence increasing after menopause. The genitourinary syndrome of menopause increases susceptibility to recurrent urinary tract infections through urogenital atrophy and microbiome disruption, compounding the risk of antimicrobial resistance.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesise evidence on digital health technologies for the prevention and management of urinary tract infections in menopausal women.
METHODS: Four databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane) were systematically searched from January 2000 to March 2026 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Study quality was assessed using risk-of-bias and critical appraisal tools. Menopausal status was classified as explicitly, proxy or not reported.
RESULTS: Of 9935 records identified, 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Four technology clusters emerged: patient-facing digital interventions (n = 4), predictive machine-learning models (n = 7), clinician-facing electronic health record-integrated decision support systems (n = 2), and point-of-care biosensors (n = 1). Digital tools reduced inappropriate antibiotic prescribing by up to 60% and ciprofloxacin use by 80.5%. Predictive models achieved discrimination values of 0.57-0.96 but lacked prospective validation. No study applied formal staging criteria for reproductive aging or integrated hormonal variables. Time to diagnosis and treatment were not assessed.
CONCLUSIONS: Digital health technologies show potential for antimicrobial stewardship in menopausal women with urinary tract infections but remain largely insensitive to menopause-specific biological factors. One randomised controlled trial demonstrated increased uptake of vaginal oestrogen therapy with the use of these technologies, providing evidence of digitally supported non-antibiotic prevention. Future research should integrate menopausal staging, hormonal variables, and user-centred design.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251052764.

title: A 12-week randomized controlled trial of the dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH) diet in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis: Effects on disease activity and outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Dietary interventions may improve rheumatoid arthritis (RA) outcomes through anti-inflammatory and metabolic pathways. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on disease activity and treatment outcomes in patients with seropositive RA.
METHODS: In this 12-week parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 82 patients with seropositive RA were randomly assigned to a DASH diet intervention (n = 40) or a control group maintaining their usual diet (n = 42). The primary outcome was change in disease activity assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS-28 E SR). Secondary outcomes included change in DAS-28 based on C-reactive protein (DAS-28 CRP), as well as tender and swollen joint counts, ESR, CRP, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for pain and general health, the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), and the Short Form-36 (SF-36). Adherence to the intervention was evaluated using the DASH diet score. Assessments were performed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Data were analyzed according to the intention-to-treat principle. Repeated clinical outcomes were analyzed using robust mixed ANOVA or generalized estimating equations (GEE), as appropriate.
RESULTS: Of the 82 randomized patients, 49 completed the 12-week study. Adherence to the DASH diet increased significantly in the intervention group compared with the control group (p < 0.001). From baseline to Week 12, DAS-28 ESR decreased by 0.92 points in the DASH group versus 0.17 points in the control group, corresponding to a 0.75-point greater reduction (group × time interaction, p = 0.001). Significant between-group differences in change were also observed for DAS-28 CRP (-0.62), ESR (-3.90 mm/h), VAS-pain (-2.19), VAS-general health (-2.12), and HAQ (-0.38) (all group × time p˂0.05). For SF-36, significant between-group differences in change were observed for physical functioning (+10.15), role-physical (+47.30), bodily pain (+22.17), vitality (+18.52), role-emotional (+38.61), and mental health (+12.06) (all group × time p < 0.05). CRP, tender and swollen joint counts did not show significant group × time interactions (p > 0.05). Furthermore, in the intervention group, improvements in DASH diet adherence were negatively correlated with changes in DAS-28 ESR and DAS-28 CRP scores (both p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: A 12-week DASH dietary intervention may provide clinically meaningful improvements in disease activity and patient-reported outcomes in patients with seropositive RA. These findings support the potential role of the DASH dietary pattern as a promising dietary approach to complement the management of RA. However, the relatively high attrition rate should be considered when interpreting the findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered with Clinicaltrials.gov (ID: NCT07170033). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07170033.

title: Medical cannabis for the treatment of insomnia.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

publication_events.note: Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2025 Apr 03;4:CD016216. doi: 10.1002/14651858.CD016216.

abstract:
RATIONALE: Insomnia is highly prevalent and associated with substantial individual and societal burden, while existing pharmacological treatments are limited by adverse effects and concerns about long-term use. The role of medical cannabis in the treatment of insomnia remains unclear because of limited and heterogeneous evidence. Despite increasing clinical use, current guidelines do not provide clear recommendations due to uncertainty regarding its efficacy and safety. A clear synthesis of available evidence is needed to inform patients, clinicians, and policymakers about the potential benefits and harms of medical cannabis for insomnia.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of medical cannabis in adults with insomnia.
SEARCH METHODS: We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, Global Index Medicus, and two trial registers, together with reference checking, citation searching, and contacting study authors, to identify studies for inclusion in the review. The latest search date was 5 April 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included parallel randomized controlled trials (RCTs), cross-over RCTs, and cluster RCTs in adult participants with any type of insomnia comparing medical cannabis with placebo, benzodiazepine receptor agonists, benzodiazepines, melatonin receptor agonists, antidepressants, and antipsychotics. We excluded studies that were quasi-RCTs and studies using experimental and unregistered drugs, cannabis receptor antagonists and negative allosteric modulators like rimonabant, as well as modulators that enhance endocannabinoid system activity, such as fatty acid amide hydrolase inhibitors, and synthetic cannabis, like levonantradol.
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep, total sleep time and adverse events. Our important outcomes included sleep onset latency, wake after sleep onset, daytime functioning, withdrawal symptoms, and quality of life.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for parallel RCTs and the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for cross-over RCTs.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesized results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible, using a random-effects model. Where this was not possible due to the nature of the data, we synthesized results narratively. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for our critical outcomes, daytime functioning and quality of life for the comparison of medical cannabis versus placebo.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included nine studies with 537 participants aged 18 to 76 years. Most studies included predominantly female populations (72.66%), focused mainly on participants with primary insomnia, although one study focused on insomnia associated with comorbidities. Three studies included patients with acute insomnia, and six included patients with chronic insomnia. One study compared medical cannabis with antidepressants (amitriptyline), while the other eight studies compared medical cannabis with a placebo. Two studies used licensed medications (one plant-based cannabinoid, one synthetic cannabinoid), and the other seven studies used magistral preparations.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Medical cannabis versus placebo The synthesized evidence from our comparison indicates that, compared with placebo, medical cannabis may have little to no clinically meaningful effect on the quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep (SMD -0.49, 95%CI -1.06 to 0.08, I2 = 91%; 7 studies, 374 participants, very low-certainty evidence), total sleep time (MD 7.68 minutes, 95% CI -23.04 to 38.39; I2 = 80%; 6 studies, 194 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and daytime functioning (SMD -0.34, 95% CI -0.83 to 0.16; I2 = 65%, 5 studies, 144 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and may improve quality of life (SMD 0.84, 95% CI -0.61 to 2.29; I2 = 78%; 3 studies, 95 participants; very low-certainty evidence), but the evidence is very uncertain. Additionally, medical cannabis may result in a slight increase in adverse events (OR 11.25, 95% CI 4.46 to 28.35; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 98 participants; low-certainty evidence; participants with adverse events in the intervention period: 37; in the placebo period: 0; in both periods: 14; in neither period: 47). The main reasons for downgrading the certainty of the evidence were high risk of bias, serious inconsistency, and imprecision.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Medical cannabis may have little to no clinically meaningful effect on quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep, total sleep time, or daytime functioning. It may lead to an improvement in quality of life, although the evidence is very uncertain. Medical cannabis may result in a slight increase in adverse events, but the certainty of this evidence is low. Future research must address the substantial uncertainty in the current evidence by conducting adequately powered, well-designed randomized trials with longer follow-up, standardized outcomes, and detailed reporting of efficacy and safety, including long-term harms. In addition, studies should explicitly incorporate equity considerations by enrolling more diverse populations and reporting disaggregated data by sex, age, and other relevant characteristics to improve the applicability and fairness of the evidence base.
FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.
REGISTRATION: Protocol: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD016216.

title: Analgesic efficacy of uni-level erector spinae plane block in breast cancer surgery patients: a systematic review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgery remains the cornerstone of management in breast cancer patients. Regional anesthesia techniques, such as the erector spinae plane block (ESPB), have emerged as adjuncts to standard therapy for postoperative pain control.
METHODS: Studies comparing ESPB and standard procedure of general anesthesia and opioids were included. Primary outcomes were postoperative pain scores, analgesia duration, and postoperative morphine consumption.
RESULTS: VAS pain scores were significantly reduced with the ESPB group. Similarly, longer analgesia duration (MD 7.03, 95%CI 4.92, 9.14, P < 0.0001), and lower postoperative morphine consumption (MD -5.77; 95% CI, -7.89, -3.65; P < 0.0001) were observed in the ESPB group. NRS pain scores at 24 h, intraoperative fentanyl, and postoperative tramadol consumption also decreased with ESPB. No significant differences were observed for NRS scores at 12 h. However, heterogeneity was high and most of the included studies had high or unclear risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: ESPB may reduce opioid consumption and postoperative pain scores compared to the control groups. However, these results should be taken cautiously, due to the high risk of bias among the included studies and low certainty.

title: Magnesium sulfate versus dexmedetomidine as adjuvants for peribulbar block: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Regional anesthesia is widely used for ophthalmic surgery, but peribulbar block may have slower onset and variable akinesia. Dexmedetomidine and magnesium sulfate are used as adjuvants, yet their comparative effects remain uncertain.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 and Cochrane guidance (PROSPERO CRD420261435378). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane and Google Scholar were searched from inception to May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing magnesium sulfate with dexmedetomidine as adjuvants to peribulbar local anesthetic. Random-effects meta-analysis used REML, conventional and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals, prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, dosage and surgery-based subgroup analyses, and GRADE assessment.
RESULTS: Six randomized controlled trials were included. Most pooled outcomes showed no statistically significant between-group differences, including sensory-block onset (MD - 0.04 min, 95% CI - 0.15 to 0.06), globe-akinesia onset (MD - 0.33 min, 95% CI - 1.61 to 0.96), globe-akinesia duration (MD - 11.46 min, 95% CI - 29.68 to 6.77), time to block adequacy (MD 0.10 min, 95% CI - 0.92 to 1.12), IOP at 5 and 10 min, akinesia scores, supplementary injection, and satisfaction. Dexmedetomidine was associated with faster lid-akinesia onset in the conventional analysis (MD 0.32 min, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.50; P = 0.0003), but the HK-adjusted CI crossed the null (- 0.31 to 0.95). Conventional analyses also favored dexmedetomidine for lid-akinesia duration (MD - 12.20 min, P = 0.0188) and time to first analgesia (MD - 18.22 min, P = 0.0101), but both lost statistical significance after HK adjustment. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes, and GRADE certainty ranged from high to very low, with most outcomes rated very low.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not establish a clear efficacy or safety advantage of magnesium sulfate or dexmedetomidine as a peribulbar adjuvant. Apparent benefits for lid-akinesia onset, lid-akinesia duration, and time to first analgesia are sensitive to conservative statistical adjustment and should not be interpreted as definitive. The evidence base is small, heterogeneous, geographically concentrated, and generally low or very low certainty; adequately powered multicenter trials with standardized dosing and outcome assessment are needed.

title: The Impact of Plasmapheresis on Serum Concentrations of Antiseizure Medications: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Seizures are an important neurological manifestation of several autoimmune and antibody-mediated disorders and often require treatment with antiseizure medications (ASMs). Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) is frequently used to treat these antibody-mediated conditions by removing circulating pathogenic factors. However, TPE is non-selective and may also remove protein-bound ASMs, particularly those with low volume of distribution. This unintended drug clearance may result in subtherapeutic concentrations and breakthrough seizures. This study aims to systematically assess the available evidence on the effects of TPE on ASM serum concentrations. It also seeks to determine whether drug removal is clinically significant and needs post-procedure supplemental dosing. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane Library from April to May 2025 using predefined MeSH terms and keywords related to epilepsy, ASMs, and TPE. Randomized trials and case reports/series involving patients receiving ASMs concomitantly with TPE and reporting serum drug concentrations were included. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. The primary outcome was the effect of TPE on ASM serum concentrations and the need for dose adjustment. Eighteen studies comprising 30 patients were included. Phenytoin was the most frequently evaluated ASM; although total serum concentrations often declined during TPE, overall drug removal was generally low, and free levels frequently remained therapeutic. Phenobarbital showed minimal change, while valproate and several newer ASMs demonstrated variable reductions in serum concentrations. Breakthrough seizures were reported in seven studies, ranging from transient events to refractory seizures requiring dose adjustments or treatment discontinuation. The effect of TPE on ASM pharmacokinetics was found to be drug-specific and largely influenced by protein binding and volume of distribution. Although overall drug removal is generally limited, peri-procedural serum fluctuations may contribute to breakthrough seizures in vulnerable patients. Routine supplemental dosing is not generally recommended; instead, individualized monitoring, and post-session dosing strategies are advised, particularly for ASMs with low volume of distribution or in high-risk patients.

title: Opioid-free versus opioid-based anesthesia for robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a single-center randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia is standard in urological surgery, and there is additional interest in eliminating intraoperative opioids in prostate cancer surgery. Randomized evidence for opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) in robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is lacking. In this single-center randomized controlled trial, adult men undergoing RARP were allocated 1:1 to OFA (dexmedetomidine plus ketamine, no intraoperative opioids) or a remifentanil-based technique. Both groups received identical multimodal premedication, a bilateral quadratus lumborum block, sevoflurane maintenance and identical oxycodone patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). The primary outcome was cumulative PCA oxycodone consumption over the first 24 postoperative hours. Prespecified secondary outcomes were pain (NRS), postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), the demanded-to-delivered PCA bolus ratio, and perioperative changes in serum creatinine and white-cell count. A total of 149 patients were analyzed (OFA n=75, opioid-based n=74). Cumulative 24-h oxycodone consumption was lower with OFA (median 12.0 mg [interquartile range, IQR 6.0-22.0] vs 19.0 mg [10.5-34.0]; p=0.001), with a Hodges-Lehmann location-shift estimate of -6.0 mg (95% confidence interval, CI -10.0 to -2.0). Pain scores did not differ at any time point, and PONV was infrequent, with no significant between-group difference. Intraoperative hemodynamic adverse events (bradycardia, hypotension), perioperative white-cell count and serum creatinine did not differ between groups. In RARP delivered on a standardized multimodal and regional analgesic background, OFA reduced postoperative opioid consumption compared with a remifentanil-based technique, without a detectable difference in pain scores and with a similar safety profile.Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06380244, registered 23 April 2024.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison.
CONCLUSION: Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) mono-agonists on reward processing in animal models: a systematic review.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), indicated in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus, influences reward processing, integral to disparate mental disorders. Emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1 receptor mono-agonists (GLP-1RAs) are potential treatment strategies for select mental disorders. Herein, we systematically review preclinical research documenting how GLP-1 and GLP-1RAs may impact reward function.
METHODS: Relevant studies were identified through Web of Science, OVID (MedLINE, Embase, PsycInfo), and PubMed from database inception to June 28, 2026. Preclinical research investigating the association between GLP-1 and select GLP-1RAs and reward function was included. Reward functions assessed were food-, drug-, and sexual-related reward.
RESULTS: A total of 66 studies met inclusion and were synthesised herein. Taken together, results indicate that GLP-1 and GLP-1RAs affect measures of food-related, drug-associated, and sexual behaviours. GLP-1 administration was associated with a reduction in food intake and gross locomotor activity with respect to approaching and engaging in reward-seeking behaviours. When locally administered in selected brain regions of evaluated animal models, exenatide was associated with reduced substance use, food seeking, and sexual behaviours (p < 0.05). Similarly, liraglutide was observed to attenuate substance and food-related rewards (p < 0.05). In addition, semaglutide was demonstrated to reduce substance and sucrose intake, while dulaglutide is reported to reduce substance intake (p < 0.001).
DISCUSSION: Extant preclinical findings demonstrate a trend toward reductions in reward-associated behaviours following GLP-1RA administration. Our findings can also provide rationale and impetus for evaluating GLP-1RAs in the treatment of psychiatric disorders characterised by disturbance in hedonic function and behaviours.

title: Gut microbial dynamics and antibiotic resistance during rifaximin therapy in severe cirrhosis: a ProPILA-Rifax ancillary study.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Increasing evidence implicates gut dysbiosis in the pathophysiology of advanced cirrhosis. This is an ancillary study of the ProPILA-Rifax trial (NCT03069131), which evaluated rifaximin (RFX) as primary prophylaxis of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) in patients with severe cirrhosis. Although the combined use of RFX and lactulose is effective in preventing recurrent hepatic encephalopathy (HE), its longitudinal impact on microbial communities and antibiotic resistance remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: We characterized longitudinal changes in the gut microbiome of 42 patients (21 RFX, 21 placebo) over 12 months using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and culture-based phenotypic susceptibility testing. Exploratory analyses between patient bacterial profiles and clinical outcomes (disease severity, overall survival, and incidence of SBP) were conducted.
RESULTS: RFX treatment reduced microbial richness and decreased the abundance of taxa typically enriched in advanced cirrhosis (e.g., Escherichia, Streptococcus, Veillonella). RFX increased the proportion of Escherichia coli isolates exhibiting phenotypic resistance to rifampicin, without observed cross-resistance to ciprofloxacin or cefotaxime. In exploratory analyses, a decrease in Child-Pugh scores was correlated with enrichment of commensal taxa. Moreover, higher abundances of Ruminococcus bromii and Blautia obeum at inclusion were respectively associated with improved 12-month survival and a lower incidence of SBP.
DISCUSSION: In severe cirrhosis, RFX profoundly alters gut microbial composition by reducing pathobiont abundance while promoting rifampicin resistance in E. coli. Furthermore, microbiota-derived signatures were associated with Child-Pugh scores, highlighting their potential to improve patient stratification.

title: Ilioinguinal-Transversus Abdominis Plane (I-TAP) Block with Liposomal Bupivacaine for Analgesia After Cesarean Delivery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Cesarean delivery is frequently associated with suboptimal postoperative analgesia. While PROSPECT guidelines recommend transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block for post-cesarean analgesia, conventional TAP block may provide incomplete coverage of the L1 dermatome, potentially limiting analgesia for lower abdominal incisions. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided ilioinguinal-transversus abdominis plane (I-TAP) block with liposomal bupivacaine after cesarean delivery.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, 150 healthy parturients undergoing elective cesarean delivery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia were allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to I-TAP block, transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block, or sham block. The I-TAP and TAP blocks were performed using a mixture of 266 mg liposomal bupivacaine and 50 mg bupivacaine hydrochloride, diluted with 0.9% sodium chloride to a total volume of 60 mL. The primary outcome was the cumulative intravenous sufentanil consumption from the patient controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) device during the first 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included 48 h PCIA sufentanil requirements, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) scores, pain scores, time to first rescue analgesia, time to ambulation, successful breastfeeding initiation, maternal satisfaction, and adverse events.
RESULTS: At 24 h postoperatively, the I-TAP group had significantly lower sufentanil consumption than the TAP group (mean difference -11.4 μg, 95% CI: -17.6 to -5.3; 37.1% reduction) and the control group (mean difference -23.2 μg, 95% CI: -29.4 to -17.1; 54.5% reduction) (both P < 0.001). This difference persisted at 48 h. The I-TAP group also had lower postoperative pain scores, higher QoR-15 scores, longer time to first opioid rescue request, higher maternal satisfaction and higher rate of successful breastfeeding initiation. Adverse events were similar among groups.
CONCLUSION: Compared with TAP block plus epidural hydromorphone and epidural hydromorphone alone, liposomal bupivacaine I-TAP block combined with epidural hydromorphone significantly reduced post-cesarean PCIA sufentanil requirements, improved postoperative analgesia and recovery quality, and increased maternal satisfaction without evidence of increased adverse events. This technique may provide a safe and effective option for implementation within multimodal analgesic strategy after cesarean delivery.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER AND REGISTRY: ChiCTR2500112390.

title: Effects of Sodium Bicarbonate Ringer's Solution versus Lactate Ringer's Solution on Emergence Time in Patients Undergoing Supratentorial Tumor Resection: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In neuroanesthesia, a prompt emergence from anesthesia is essential for postoperative neurologic assessment. Intraoperative infusion of sodium bicarbonate Ringer's solution (BRS) and lactated Ringer's solution (LRS) have different effects on internal environment, potentially contributing to discrepant recovery profiles. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the recovery of BRS and LRS in patients undergoing craniotomy for supratentorial tumors.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial enrolled patients undergoing elective supratentorial tumor resection. Patients were randomized to receive BRS or LRS for intraoperative fluid therapy. The primary outcome was emergence time. Secondary outcomes included extubation times, short Orientation Memory Concentration Test (SOMCT) at 15 min after extubation and postoperative complications. Parameters including lactic acid (Lac), pH, base excess (BE), and serum Mg2+ levels were measured at several time points and compared between the two groups. Total length of hospital stay was also recorded and compared between the two groups. Primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle. A per-protocol (PP) sensitivity analysis was also performed for the primary outcome.
RESULTS: The ITT analysis included 100 patients (BRS group: n = 50; LRS group: n = 50). Following exclusions for short surgery or massive intraoperative blood loss, the PP set included 48 BRS and 47 LRS patients. In the ITT analysis, Patients assigned to the BRS group had shorter emergence (13min vs 16min; median difference, 3; 95% CI, 1 to 4; P=0.003) and extubation times (15min vs 18min; median difference, 2; 95% CI, 1 to 4; P=0.01), and lower lactate levels at the end of surgery and 0.5 hour after extubation (P < 0.05). SOMCT scores at 15 min after extubation, postoperative complications and total hospitalization days were comparable between the groups (P > 0.05). Additionally, no significant group-by-time interactions were found for pH, BE and Mg2⁺ levels, indicating similar temporal changes between groups (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Patients receiving BRS during supratentorial tumor resection had faster emergence and shorter extubation times, but similar SOMCT scores at 15 min after extubation and complication rates compared to those receiving LRS.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500105691, registered on July 9, 2025.

title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care.
OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.
RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.
CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point.
RESULTS: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2).
CONCLUSIONS: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

title: Evidence on Glutathione and Boosters for Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) adversely affects treatment efficacy and quality of life. Despite studies on glutathione (GSH) or GSH boosters' antioxidative effects for prevention, optimal management remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to consolidate and critically appraise the current evidence and to compare the efficacy of GSH and GSH boosters for the prevention of CIPN. The MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL databases were searched through March 2025. Twenty-five RCTs involving 1625 patients were included. No intervention significantly reduced all-grade CIPN compared with placebo. N-acetylcysteine (odds ratio [OR] 0.19, 95% credible intervals [CrI] 0.05-0.63), GSH (OR 0.34, 95% CrI 0.13-0.79) and vitamin E (OR 0.33, 95% CrI 0.11-0.91) were associated with a reduced incidence of grade 3/4 CIPN compared with placebo. N-acetylcysteine ranked highest for both all-grade and grade 3/4 CIPN prevention. These findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with pre-existing neuropathy but were not retained in analyses restricted to double-blind studies. Overall, N-acetylcysteine, GSH, and vitamin E were associated with potential reductions in severe CIPN, with N-acetylcysteine consistently ranking highest, although these associations should be regarded as preliminary. Further rigorously conducted and adequately powered trials are warranted to confirm these findings and evaluate agents demonstrating potential benefits.

title: Carbonyl reductase 1 regulates prednisolone clearance and modifies its adverse effect profile.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prednisolone is widely prescribed but associated with marked interindividual variability in adverse effects. While 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (11β-HSD) enzymes regulate glucocorticoid (GC) activation, the contribution of alternative clearance pathways remains unclear. We aimed to characterize prednisolone metabolism beyond 11β-HSD enzymes, define the roles of carbonyl reductase 1 (CBR-1) and AKR1C1, and assess the clinical relevance of specific metabolites.
DESIGN: Post hoc targeted metabolomic analysis of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial combined with mechanistic in vitro overexpression studies.
METHODS: Thirty healthy male volunteers from the TICSI trial (NCT03111810) and HEK293 cells overexpressing CBR-1 or AKR1C1 were studied. Participants received prednisolone (20 mg daily for 1 week) with placebo or the selective 11β-HSD1 inhibitor AZD4017. In vitro, transfected HEK293 cells were treated with prednisolone or prednisone. Steroid metabolites were quantified by targeted LC-MS/MS, and associations with glucose disposal and osteocalcin were assessed.
RESULTS: 20β-reduced metabolites were major contributors to prednisolone clearance. In vitro, CBR-1 preferentially reduced prednisone, with 20β-dihydro-prednisone accounting for up to 78% of its clearance, whereas AKR1C1 had minimal impact. In vivo, 11β-HSD1 inhibition reduced prednisolone exposure without a compensatory rise in prednisone, with a relative increase in CBR-1-mediated 20β-reduction. Higher circulating 20β-dihydro-prednisone at 4 h independently predicted improved glucose disposal and higher osteocalcin levels.
CONCLUSIONS: CBR-1 is a key determinant of prednisolone and prednisone clearance in humans and is associated with clinically relevant metabolic and skeletal outcomes. Circulating 20β-dihydro-prednisone may serve as an informative biomarker of GC exposure and adverse effect risk, supporting metabolite-guided approaches to GC therapy.

title: Formulation-Dependent Modulation of Ibuprofen Absorption Kinetics in Fixed-Dose Combinations: An Exploratory Analysis of the Dissolution-Absorption Relationship.
abstract: We conducted a pharmacokinetic study to compare two fixed-dose combinations of ibuprofen/acetaminophen (IP-TA and IP-TB) with different formulation designs and excipient compositions, and explored how formulation differences influence ibuprofen pharmacokinetics by comparing in vitro dissolution and in vivo absorption profiles. In an open-label, randomized, 2-treatment, 2-period, 2-sequence crossover study, 24 healthy Japanese participants received a single oral dose of IP-TA (ibuprofen 195 mg and acetaminophen 195 mg) or IP-TB (ibuprofen 160 mg and acetaminophen 160 mg) under fasting conditions. Pharmacokinetic data were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. Fraction absorbed (Fa) was estimated using the Loo-Riegelman method, and ibuprofen dissolution was evaluated at pH 1.2, 4.0, and 6.8. The relationship between weighted mean dissolution rates (D) and Fa was examined. Ibuprofen absorption from IP-TA was faster than from IP-TB, as reflected by higher Cmax and greater early exposure, and these differences remained after dose normalization. Dissolution profiles showed temporal similarity with absorption profiles, particularly for IP-TA. Analysis of Fa also suggested a relatively high degree of synchronization between ibuprofen and acetaminophen absorption in IP-TA. These findings indicate that formulation-dependent differences in dissolution behavior may influence early ibuprofen absorption, although further studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms.

title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome: a single-center case series and systematic review.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of our study was to evaluate the clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, and prognostic features of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome (IM3OS).
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of seven patients with IM3OS treated at Hospital del Mar between 2020 and 2025, together with a systematic review and descriptive patient-level synthesis of the published literature. PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase were searched for reports published between 2015 and 2025, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included case reports, case series, letters, correspondence, and conference abstracts providing sufficient individual patient-level data.
RESULTS: In our series, all seven patients were male, with a median age of 81 years. The most frequent tumor types were non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (42.8%) and urothelial carcinoma (28.5%). Diplopia (71.4%), ptosis (71.4%), and dyspnea (71.4%) were the most common presenting manifestations. Most patients received high-dose corticosteroids (71.4%), intravenous immunoglobulins (85.7%), and additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents (85.7%). The systematic review included 71 studies and 103 patients. Median age was 71 years, and 68.9% were male. Melanoma (35.9%), renal cell carcinoma (16.5%), and NSCLC (16.5%) were the most frequent malignancies. Ptosis (71.8%) and weakness (62.1%) were the most common presenting symptoms. The most frequently reported initial regimen was methylprednisolone 1 g/day (35.9%), and 52.4% of patients received additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents.
CONCLUSION: IM3OS is a rare, early-onset, clinically severe immune-related overlap syndrome with a high mortality rate requiring prompt recognition, structured multisystem assessment, close cardiorespiratory monitoring, and multidisciplinary management. Current evidence remains observational and does not allow conclusions regarding therapeutic superiority.

title: Laser Therapy for Sexual Health in Breast Cancer Survivors Receiving Aromatase Inhibitors: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Laser therapy is increasingly used to treat genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) in breast cancer survivors, but sham-controlled evidence of benefit remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 12-month efficacy and safety of fractional carbon dioxide (CO2) laser therapy (CLT) vs sham laser therapy (SLT) for GSM in breast cancer survivors receiving aromatase inhibitors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This is a secondary analysis of a single-center, double-blind, sham-controlled randomized clinical trial conducted at a tertiary academic hospital in Spain. Participants included breast cancer survivors with GSM and dyspareunia receiving aromatase inhibitors, recruited from October 30, 2020, to September 1, 2021. Participants were followed up for 12 months. Data were analyzed from December 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Five monthly sessions of CLT or SLT plus first-line nonhormonal therapy (FLT), including vaginal moisturizers and vibrators.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) score. Secondary outcomes included rate of sexual activity, dyspareunia, Spanish Body Image Scale, quality of life (12-Item Short Form Health Survey), Vaginal Health Index, objective parameters (pH, vaginal maturation index, epithelial measures), serum estradiol level, FLT adherence, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Of the 84 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [8.8] years), 67 completed the 12-month follow-up (CLT, 32; SLT, 35). The CLT group did not differ from the SLT group in FSFI score change from baseline to 12 months (difference, CLT vs SLT, -0.69 [95% CI, -3.58 to 2.20]; P = .64), nor in any secondary outcome. Across the full sample, significant improvements from baseline to 12 months were observed in FSFI score (18.9 to 23.0; mean difference, 4.5 [95% CI, 3.1-5.9]; P < .001), dyspareunia (mean difference, -3.7 [95% CI, -4.4 to -3.0]; P < .001), Spanish Body Image Scale (mean difference, -3.9 [95% CI, -5.1 to -2.8]; P < .001), and Vaginal Health Index (mean difference, 4.2 [95% CI, 3.1-5.2]; P < .001). Sexual activity increased among 57 of 67 participants (85.1%; odds ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.23-4.50]; P = .009). Improvements were found in pH (mean difference, -0.5 [95% CI, -0.8 to -0.2]; P < .001) and vaginal maturation index (mean difference, 19.0% [95% CI, 13.4%-24.5%]; P < .001). FLT adherence was similar between groups. No severe adverse effects occurred.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial of breast cancer survivors receiving aromatase inhibitors, vulvovaginal CLT provided no additional benefit for sexual or vaginal health at 12 months. Improvements in both groups likely reflected FLT adherence, trial participation, or contextual factors rather than laser efficacy. High-quality sham-controlled trials remain essential before routine implementation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04619485.

title: The impact of prophylactic azithromycin on the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome.
abstract: Early-life antibiotic exposure can profoundly impact the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome, with short- and long-term consequences for health. In a large multi-center (n = 28) study of 693 preterm infants, we investigated the effects of 10 d of prophylactic intravenous azithromycin on the gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The AZithromycin ThErapy for Chronic Lung Disease of Prematurity (AZTEC) study was a double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of preterm infants (born < 30 weeks of gestation), treated from birth for 10 d with either intravenous azithromycin or placebo, and sampled longitudinally for 21 d or discharge. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and quantitative PCR, we show azithromycin reduced microbial diversity and the relative abundance of health-associated Bifidobacterium and increased relative abundances of pathobionts Staphylococcus and Enterobacter/Klebsiella. This early azithromycin treatment increased the number of macrolide-resistant genes, including the presence of erm (C), which persisted for the duration of the study. Probiotic use (at individual unit discretion) increased alpha diversity and Bifidobacterium relative abundance, but did not fully mitigate the effects of azithromycin receipt. Combined azithromycin and probiotics further increased the enrichment of Enterobacter/Klebsiella and total ARGs, including erm(C). These findings highlight the impacts of antibiotic and probiotic use, both important in balancing infection control issues and microbiome disruption and antimicrobial resistance.

title: Effects of ADHD Medications on Male Reproductive Function: A Systematic Review of In Vivo Mammalian Evidence.
abstract: Long-term treatment with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) medications may begin before reproductive maturity, but their effects on male reproductive health remain uncertain. We systematically evaluated controlled in vivo mammalian evidence on male reproductive effects of medications used for ADHD, including the consistency, timing, reversibility, and certainty of reported associations. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 8 August 2026. Eligible studies were English-language, controlled in vivo mammalian experiments evaluating a prespecified ADHD medication and at least one male reproductive outcome. Human, in-vitro-only, uncontrolled, conference-abstract, and preprint reports were excluded. Risk of bias was independently assessed by two reviewers using the Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation (SYRCLE) tool, and certainty was evaluated using an adapted preclinical Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Results were grouped by drug and nine prespecified outcome domains and synthesized narratively. Meta-analysis was not performed because of substantial methodological and outcome heterogeneity. Twenty-two studies were included: 19 evaluated methylphenidate (MPH), two clonidine, and one lisdexamfetamine (LDX); 17 were conducted in rats, four in mice, and one in rhesus macaques. During active MPH exposure, adverse changes predominated in spermatogenesis, sperm quantity or quality, testicular or epididymal microstructure, testosterone, and apoptotic or inflammatory markers. Findings after drug-free follow-up were more often neutral, mixed, or partially reversible. Possible persistent sperm DNA fragmentation and adverse paternal embryonic outcomes were reported but were based on few studies with clustering concerns. Clonidine studies indicated altered epididymal contractility and transport, whereas the single high-dose LDX study reported adverse sperm, testicular, endocrine, DNA-fragmentation, and inflammatory findings. Risk-of-bias assessments were dominated by unclear judgments. None of the 18 drug-by-outcome-domain bodies of evidence reached high or moderate certainty; all were rated as very low certainty. Evidence was limited by small samples, heterogeneous species, developmental stages, doses, routes, exposure durations and assays, incomplete numerical reporting, serious indirectness to therapeutic use in men, and sparse replication outside MPH. ADHD medications, particularly MPH during active exposure, show a possible male reproductive toxicity signal in animal models, but the evidence does not permit quantitative risk estimation or class-wide or clinical conclusions. Better-controlled, exposure-validated animal studies and prospective human cohorts are needed.

title: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal samples collected from patients enrolled in the original clinical trial to investigate whether Micodigest® supplementation was associated with changes in the functional potential of the gut microbiome. A total of 37 patients were analyzed, including 24 receiving Micodigest® and 13 receiving placebo, with paired samples collected before supplementation and after 4-6 weeks of intervention. Shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed, and microbial functional potential was characterized using KEGG Orthologues (KOs). Differential abundance analysis identified 14 significantly different KOs between groups at baseline and 23 after intervention, with no overlap between the two sets of orthologues. Following supplementation, Micodigest®-treated patients exhibited increased representation of functions related to CRISPR-associated systems, bacteriophage biology, and chitin-derived carbohydrate utilization, together with reduced representation of nutrient acquisition systems, conjugative transfer, sulfur metabolism, and components of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. These functional signatures suggest coordinated changes in microbial ecological adaptation, nutrient utilization, genetic exchange, and metabolic activity following fungal nutraceutical supplementation. Integration with previously reported taxonomic and inflammatory findings supports the hypothesis that Micodigest® may promote coordinated remodeling of the gut microbiome and host-microbiota interactions during the perioperative period. Although the present study cannot establish causality or directly infer microbial activity from metagenomic potential, these findings provide novel functional insights into the microbiome response to fungal nutraceutical supplementation in patients with CRC and highlight functional metagenomics as a valuable complement to taxonomic profiling.

title: Synbiotic HQP08 Supplementation for Hair Loss and Depressive Symptoms: An Open-Label Pilot Study of Clinical Outcomes and Gut Microbiome Changes.
abstract: Background: Gut microbiota dysregulation has been implicated in hair loss via the gut-skin axis, but human interventional data are limited. We previously showed that Bifidobacterium longum HK003 reverses alopecia-like phenotypes in mice. Methods: We conducted an open-label, single-arm pilot study to evaluate an HK003-containing synbiotic (HQP08) in 32 adults with self-reported hair loss over 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants reporting improvement on the Patient Global Impression of Change (PGI-C) scale at week 8. Secondary outcomes included changes in hair loss severity, 60 s hair count, depressive symptoms (PHQ-9), safety, and gut microbiome composition (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2500112698). Results: At week 8, 62.5% (20/32) of participants reported PGI-C improvement. Significant reductions were observed in hair loss severity (p = 0.0008), 60 s hair count (p = 0.0048), and PHQ-9 scores (p = 0.002). Younger age was associated with PGI-C response (OR per year 0.86, 95% CI: 0.73-0.98, p = 0.037). Metagenomic analysis identified engraftment of B. longum HK003-like profiles in a subset of participants at week 12. Changes in microbial pathways related to thiamine metabolism, vitamin B12 salvage, and lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis were associated with ΔPHQ-9 (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05), but not with hair-related endpoints. No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions: This first-in-human pilot study suggests that HQP08 was well tolerated and was associated with within-participant changes in hair-loss measurements and PHQ-9 scores. Randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm efficacy and further elucidate mechanisms within the gut-brain-skin axis.
