title: Compression therapy in the prevention of thromboembolic disease following total knee arthroplasty with a fast recovery protocol: A systematic review.
abstract: Thromboembolic disease (TED), including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), remains a serious postoperative risk after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols emphasize early mobilization, warranting reassessment of mechanical prophylaxis, such as compression therapy. This systematic review evaluates the benefits of compression therapy in preventing TED in TKA patients under ERAS protocols combined with pharmacological prophylaxis. A systematic review was conducted, analyzing seven studies comparing combined mechanical and pharmacological prophylaxis with pharmacological prophylaxis alone. Primary outcomes included DVT and PE incidence, compliance, adverse events, and efficacy. Seven studies were included in this systematic review, including 871 patients. Combined mechanical and pharmacological prophylaxis reduced DVT rates. Continuous enhanced circulation therapy (CECT) with enoxaparin lowered DVT from 19.5% to 6.6% (relative risk reduction (RRR) 66.2%, p=0.018), while intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) with rivaroxaban reduced rates from 18.3% to 8.3% (RRR 54.5%, p<0.01). Pneumatic plantar compression (PPC) decreased DVT from 67% to 27% in unilateral and 52% to 28% in bilateral TKA (combined RRR 54.2%, p<0.001). Graduated compression stockings (GCS) with anticoagulation reduced DVT from 13.0% to 6.0% (RRR 53.8%, p=0.0872). IPC with nadroparin lowered DVT from 3.9% to 2.6% (RRR 33.3%, p=0.65). PE incidence remained minimal across studies. When combined with anticoagulants, mechanical prophylaxis may have an additional role in diminishing DVT incidence while alleviating postoperative swelling and pain. However, optimizing compliance, standardizing protocols, and tailoring thromboprophylaxis to patient-specific risks remain key challenges. Future research should refine mechanical and pharmacological strategies to enhance safety, efficacy, and recovery in TKA patients.

title: Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy in Kidney Transplant Recipients: an Updated Systematic Review and Surgical Perspective>.
journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Persistent hyperparathyroidism and calcitriol deficiency coexist in most long -term kidney transplant recipients, yet the combined skeletal effects of these presentations have not been formally quantified.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross -sectional analytical study at People's Hospital 115 (Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam ), we studied 135 kidney transplant recipients (mean age 51.0 ± 11.3 years; 66.7 % male; mean time posttransplant 71.4 ± 28.1 months ) who underwent simultaneous measurement of serum intact parathyroid hormone, 1,25 -dihydroxyvitamin D, and dual -energy x -ray absorptiometry at 3 skeletal sites. A prespecified piecewise ordinary least -squares model characterized the relationship between parathyroid hormone and bone mineral density; a confirmatory sensitivity analysis used KDIGO -motivated breakpoint of 65 pg /mL for parathyroid hormone. We evaluated parathyroid hormone -to -vitamin D ratio as a prespecified secondary exposure measure.
RESULTS: Bone loss (worst -site T score of < -1.0 ) was present in 103 participants (76.3 % ) and osteoporosis in 27 (20.0 % ). The confirmatory piecewise model at 65 pg /mL demonstrated that above -threshold parathyroid hormone was inversely associated with T -score composite ( β = -0.00367 per pg /mL; bootstrap 95 % CI, -0.0066 to -0.0013; P < .001 ), a 100 pg /mL increment above the threshold corresponded to a -0.37 T -score decrement. Body mass index was the strongest predictor (β = +0.129 per kg /m ²; P < .001 ). The ratio of parathyroid hormone to vitamin D (ρ = -0.262; P = .002 ) provided modestly better model fit than parathyroid hormone alone (R ² = 0.247 vs 0.229; change in Akaike Information Criterion = 3.2 ).
CONCLUSIONS: Parathyroid hormone exerted a threshold -dependent inverse effect on bone mineral density in long -term kidney transplant recipients, confirmed at the KDIGO lower boundary of 65 pg /mL. The ratio of parathyroid hormone to vitamin D captured the combined mineral burden more efficiently than parathyroid hormone level alone, warranting further prospective evaluation as a monitoring target in posttransplant mineral disease.

title: Long-term efficacy of lebrikizumab in treating head, neck and face involvement in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Head, neck, and face (HNF) atopic dermatitis (AD) substantially impairs quality of life, yet long-term biologic efficacy data in HNF areas remain limited.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis evaluates HNF efficacy of lebrikizumab across phase 3 trials (ADvocate 1&2, ADjoin) and targeted populations (ADmirable, ADapt) in adolescents (≥12 years, ≥40 kg) and adults with moderate-to-severe AD. Outcomes included HN EASI sub-scores and Face Investigator's Global Assessment (F-IGA).
RESULTS: Lebrikizumab 250 mg Q4W provided durable efficacy through 3 years among week 16 responders. At week 152, 94.8%, 82.9%, and 85.3% maintained HN EASI 75, 90, and 100 responses, respectively.Stable response (maintaining ≥80% of attended visits) through week 152 was observed in 88.8% (HN EASI 75), 80.0% (HN EASI 90), and 74.0% (HN EASI 100) of patients. Additionally, 93.8% achieved absolute HN EASI ≤1 and 69.2% achieved HN EASI = 0 at week 152 in week 16 responders. In ADmirable (skin of color), 61% of Lebri-treated patients achieved F-IGA 0 at week 24. In ADapt (prior dupilumab exposure), 55% achieved F-IGA 0 at week 24.
CONCLUSIONS: Lebrikizumab provided durable, stable long-term HNF efficacy across diverse populations, including systemic-naive patients and those with prior biologic exposure.

title: Cost-effectiveness of monotherapy and combination therapy for myopia control in Chinese children.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myopia poses a major public health and economic burden in China, necessitating cost-effectiveness evaluations of control strategies. We aimed to assess cost-effectiveness of single/combined myopia control in children and adolescents to optimise strategies.
METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of myopia control interventions in Chinese children (aged 6-18 years). Annual changes in axial length (AL) and spherical equivalent refraction (SER) were the primary outcomes. Additionally, we used a decision-analytic Markov model with clinical and cost data from China to evaluate 16 myopia control strategies for eight-year-old children over eight years from a patient perspective, with 3% discounting. Strategies included monotherapies and combined therapies. Main outcomes were incremental cost per unit reduction in myopic shift (i.e. SER) or AL elongation, compared with single-vision lenses (SVLs). Markov cohort analysis simulated the proportion of individuals progressing to high myopia under various strategies. We assessed robustness through deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses. We performed subgroup analyses by onset age (6, 10, and 12 years) and regional economic development.
RESULTS: For SER reduction, outdoor activity was cost-effective (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio = USD -18.29/dioptre (D)). At higher willingness-to-pay thresholds, 0.01% atropine combined with defocus incorporated multiple segment (DIMS) (USD 660.74/D) and repeated low-level red-light therapy (RLRL) (USD 895.36/D) were cost-effective. For AL reduction, outdoor activity (USD -42.68/mm) and DIMS (USD 672.73/mm) were cost-effective at lower thresholds, while RLRL (USD 2011.32/mm) was preferred at higher thresholds. Compared with monotherapy, combination interventions improved preventive efficacy against high myopia. Subgroup analyses confirmed that the cost-effectiveness ranking was preserved across onset ages and regional economic settings.
CONCLUSIONS: Under limited budget conditions, outdoor activities and defocus spectacles represent advantageous cost-effective treatment options. When the budget is sufficient, RLRL may be considered a promising option pending confirmation of its long-term safety and effectiveness, and 0.01% atropine combined with DIMS is the preferred cost-effective option. Our analysis provides evidence-based guidance for clinicians and families in selecting effective myopia control strategies.

title: Efficacy of Saffron as an Adjunct to Methylphenidate in Treating ADHD in Children Aged 6-12: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood disorder often managed with stimulant medications such as methylphenidate. Around 30% of patients with ADHD do not respond to treatment or cannot tolerate its side effects, which necessitates the consideration of alternative options. This study evaluated the effectiveness of adding the saffron extract to methylphenidate on ADHD symptoms and working memory in children aged 6-12.
METHOD: In a randomized clinical trial, 58 children diagnosed with ADHD were randomized into two groups: a methylphenidate (0.5-1 mg/kg/day, divided into 2-3 doses)/saffron (20-30 mg/day based on weight: 20 mg for <30 kg, 30 mg for >30 kg) group and a control group receiving only methylphenidate (0.5-1 mg/kg/day, divided into 2-3 doses) for six weeks. The severity of ADHD was evaluated using subjective (Conners' Parent Rating Scale-revised) and objective (Corsi block-span task and continuous performance test) tests at the start and end (in the sixth week) of the study.
RESULTS: 22 participants in the methylphenidate/saffron group and 21 in the control group completed the study. The changing trend of total ADHD scores (p = 0.002, Cohen's d = 0.85), hyperactivity score (p = 0.024, d = 0.62), impulsivity score (p = 0.031, d = 0.58), and attention score (p = 0.001, d = 0.92) was significantly different between groups based on subjective parent reports. However, no significant differences were found in impulsivity, inattention, or sustained attention on the CPT, though reaction time improved significantly (p = 0.023, d = 0.45). Scores on the Corsi Block Span Task indicated no significant changes in working memory between groups. The combination treatment was well-tolerated, with no reports of severe adverse effects.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that the combination of saffron with methylphenidate may enhance subjective reports of ADHD symptoms, particularly hyperactivity and impulsivity; however, objective cognitive measures showed limited changes. Given the favorable safety profile of saffron and study limitations, this supports its potential role as a complementary option, pending confirmation in placebo-controlled trials with larger samples and long-term evaluations.

title: Effects of the GnRH agonist leuprorelin on liver volume in premenopausal women with severe polycystic liver disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic liver disease (PLD) is characterized by multiple liver cysts, sometimes leading to severe liver enlargement, with associated physical and psychosocial complaints. Treatment options are limited. Female gender is a risk factor for PLD; estrogen supplementation increases liver size in women with PLD, whereas the polycystic liver decreases after menopause. Estrogens may therefore be a target for therapy.
METHODS: In this prospective, open-label study, premenopausal women aged 18-45 years with severe PLD were randomized 1:1 to a direct start of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist leuprorelin (n=6) or to standard care with delayed start of leuprorelin 18 months after randomization (n=8). The gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (11.25 mg injections once every 3 mo) leads to a reduction in estrogens and progesterone, and consequently to medically induced menopause. The primary outcome was liver growth rate at 18 months. Secondary outcomes comprised quality of life, menopausal side effects, and adverse events. An interim analysis was performed when all participants had reached month 18, as notable side effects were expressed.
RESULTS: In the group with direct start of leuprorelin, liver volume still increased in half of the participants, with the median liver growth rate not significantly different from the standard care group (4.04 [-4.62 to 6.84] vs. 11.0 [0.70-13.2] %/year, respectively, p=0.15). Importantly, PLD-related quality of life did not improve with treatment, whereas menopausal side effects were severe, leading one participant to stop treatment early. The total number of adverse events in the direct versus standard care group was 38 versus 9, respectively (p<0.001). Because of these results, the study was terminated early.
CONCLUSIONS: leuprorelin treatment did not reverse liver volume, while menopausal side effects and adverse events were substantial.

title: Prenatal statin exposure and adverse birth outcomes in Asian women: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The safety of statin use during pregnancy remains controversial. We aimed to evaluate the association between prenatal statin exposure and pregnancy outcomes in Asian women, including low birth weight, preterm birth, and congenital anomalies.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of studies in Asian populations evaluating prenatal statin exposure. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and trial registries were searched through January 31, 2026. Eligible randomized and observational studies included Asian populations and reported low birth weight, preterm birth, or congenital anomalies. Adjusted risk ratios were pooled using random-effects inverse-variance models, and risk of bias was assessed with standard tools.
RESULTS: Three nationwide observational cohort studies from Taiwan and South Korea were included in the quantitative synthesis, and one Indonesian randomized trial of pravastatin for preeclampsia prevention was reviewed qualitatively. Prenatal statin exposure was not associated with congenital anomalies (RR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.89-1.08; I2 = 0%), but was associated with low birth weight (RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49; I2 = 49%). The association with preterm birth was not statistically significant (RR, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.95-1.62; I2 = 87%). Sensitivity analyses restricted to exposed versus unexposed comparisons yielded similar conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: The available Asian evidence, largely derived from nationwide East Asian cohorts, suggests no clear association between prenatal statin exposure or continuation and congenital anomalies. A modest association with low birth weight was observed, whereas evidence for preterm birth remained inconclusive. The low-birth-weight finding should be interpreted cautiously because of residual confounding, comparator heterogeneity, prematurity-related low birth weight, and pharmacological heterogeneity across statins.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251235975.

title: An intravaginal ring for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis: assessment of safety and pharmacokinetics in a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Eastern and Southern Africa, 63% of new HIV infections occurred in women and girls, with adolescent girls and young women representing a particularly vulnerable subpopulation. Effective vaginal products for HIV prevention are desirable because they are underrepresented in the currently approved portfolio and have attributes motivating product use. In this trial, we evaluated an innovative intravaginal ring (pod-IVR) as a platform for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).
OBJECTIVE: To measure the safety and multicompartment pharmacokinetics (PKs) of a pod-IVR delivering tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) combined with emtricitabine (FTC) in healthy women over 28 days.
METHODS: The Phase 1 clinical trial consisted of a randomized order, controlled, double-blinded, crossover design. Ten women received either an active TDF-FTC pod-IVR or a placebo pod-IVR for 28 days, determined by 1:1 randomization, followed by product crossover for another 28 days. Safety was assessed in terms of adverse events related to product use, colposcopic examination, cervicovaginal epithelium thickness measurement by optical coherence tomography, and culture-independent assessment of the vaginal microbiome. Drug and/or drug metabolite concentrations were measured in cervicovaginal fluid (CVF), vaginal tissue, rectal tissue, rectal fluid, and plasma.
RESULTS: There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference in related adverse-event counts between study products. There also was no evidence suggesting the study product altered the vaginal microbiome systematically or reproducibly. Systemic plasma exposure to tenofovir (TFV) and FTC was low, consistent with topical delivery. High median CVF concentrations of TFV (38.9 ng mg-1; 135×103 fmol mg-1) and FTC (239 ng mg-1; 966×103 fmol mg-1) were measured. Median vaginal tissue concentrations of the anabolites responsible for inhibition of HIV reverse transcriptase exceeded our target concentrations: TFV diphosphate 0.651×103 fmol mg-1 and FTC triphosphate 0.180×103 fmol mg-1. Drug concentrations in rectal tissue samples generally were below the analytical lower limits of quantification, but were quantifiable in rectal fluids, 130 (TFV) and 300 (FTC) times lower than in CVF.
CONCLUSIONS: The TDF-FTC pod-IVRs were safe and well-tolerated over the 28 days of consecutive use. The PK data met the target benchmarks associated with protection from vaginal HIV infection.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03255915, identifier NCT03255915.

title: Vitiligo onset following anti-inflammatory biological therapy: a scoping review.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vitiligo is a chronic autoimmune depigmentation skin disorder characterized by the acquired loss of melanocytes, with a complex multifactorial pathophysiology. Among the potential predisposing factors, some drugs, including monoclonal antibodies, have been associated to disease onset.
METHODS: The aim of the present review is to summarize and discuss current literature findings in de novo vitiligo following biological targeting inflammatory cytokines.
RESULTS: Overall, 18 articles were considered eligible for the present review, and details of demographics, clinical characteristics, vitiligo type and localization, biological drug administered and treatment outcomes were reported.The mean age of the 39 patients was 43 years (±16.3), with a male predominance (62%). Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα) inhibitors (infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab pegol) were the most frequent suspected drugs (>50% of patients), followed by anti-IL-17A (ixekizumab, secukinumab) and anti-IL-12/23 (ustekinumab). Four cases were linked to anti-IL-4/13 (dupilumab). The median onset of vitiligo was 5 months post-initiation (range 1.5-24), with one-third of cases involving the face and neck, and two cases of segmental vitiligo. Biologic discontinuation or switching occurred in 26% of cases. Regarding outcomes, 41% experienced stabilization, 36% achieved varying degrees of repigmentation, and 8% progressed.
DISCUSSION: While de novo vitiligo is reported as a potential adverse event of biological therapies, evidence for a direct causal relationship remains weak, with cases involving non-anti-TNFα agents appearing anecdotal. The co-occurrence of underlying autoimmune comorbidities in these patients points towards a coincidental rather than a causal relationship, highlighting the need for further research to fully elucidate this association.

title: Semaglutide modulates explore/exploit decision-making in major depressive disorder: A randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Explore/exploit decision-making is a crucial component of motivated behavior. Explore/exploit behaviors are related to disparate cognitive and reward-related functions and have been implicated in multiple neuropsychiatric conditions, including major depressive disorder (MDD). Several mediators of explore/exploit decision-making have been proposed; metabolic mechanisms have been theorized to potentially affect its underlying processes. Here, we examined the effects of a GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), semaglutide, on explore/exploit behavior in patients with MDD, using a four-armed restless bandit task.
METHODS: In this secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, 72 participants with MDD were randomized either to oral semaglutide (n = 35) or placebo (n = 37), and completed the bandit task at baseline and following 16 weeks of treatment. Explore/exploit decision-making was assessed using computational modeling of choice behavior, with a trial-by-trial reinforcement-learning model.
RESULTS: Treatment with semaglutide resulted in increased exploitation (i.e. choosing the option with the highest expected reward) (Average Treatment Effect [ATE] = 0.0242, p < 0.001), directed exploration (i.e. exploring a choice with higher uncertainty) (ATE = 0.0619, p = 0.013), and perseveration (i.e. the value-independent tendency to repeat the previous action) (ATE = 0.3017, p = 0.013). These effects were moderated by, but ultimately independent of, baseline characteristics and weight loss during the trial.
CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with semaglutide modulated explore/exploit behaviors in patients with MDD. These results highlight the role of metabolic mechanisms in decision-making processes in MDD and expand knowledge of the potential neuropsychiatric effects of GLP-1RAs.

title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.
METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.
FINDINGS: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
INTERPRETATION: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.
FUNDING: The Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development.

title: B vitamins and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD): a systematic review of observational studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: B vitamins are crucial cofactors in metabolic regulation; however, their role in the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains unclear. Evidence for individual B vitamins is often contradictory. This systematic review evaluated the findings of observational studies examining the association between B vitamin intake and MASLD risk, severity, and outcomes.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published up to January 2026, adhering to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. All included studies were observational in design, encompassing cross-sectional, case-control, cohort, and Mendelian randomization (MR) studies that assessed dietary, supplemental, or biological B-vitamin status in relation to MASLD diagnoses. Study quality was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale (NOS). No quantitative meta-analysis was performed and the evidence was narratively synthesized.
RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included (38 cross-sectional, 13 case-control, 6 cohort, and 2 MR studies). Folate has been extensively studied, with most evidence suggesting a protective role for serum folate and 5-mTHF against MASLD and fibrosis. However, this was contradicted by positive associations for RBC folate and unmetabolized folic acid (UMFA). Cohort studies have linked higher folate status to reduced all-cause mortality. Vitamin B12 findings were highly controversial, with studies reporting protective, detrimental, and null associations; MR studies suggested a positive causal link with MASLD risk. Choline intake was inversely associated with steatosis but positively correlated with fibrosis in specific subgroups, including men and postmenopausal women. Evidence for niacin and pyridoxine was inconsistent, though often suggesting an inverse relationship with MASLD.
CONCLUSION: Observational evidence suggests significant, albeit contradictory, associations between specific B-vitamins (particularly folate and B12), choline, and MASLD progression. However, given the massive methodological heterogeneity and heavy reliance on cross-sectional data, the certainty of these findings is very low. The inherent uncertainty of these associations rather than concluding a probable clinical benefit should also be emphasized. Rigorous prospective cohorts and randomized controlled trials are required to establish causality and clarify the true clinical utility of B-vitamin status in MASLD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

title: Efficacy and safety of acute-phase immunotherapy for adult autoimmune encephalitis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the central nervous system associated with substantial morbidity. Acute-phase immunotherapy is crucial for improving outcomes, yet the comparative efficacy and safety of available regimens remain unclear. We therefore performed a Bayesian network meta-analysis to compare acute-phase immunotherapeutic strategies for AE.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 2025 for studies evaluating acute-phase immunotherapy in AE. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was conducted. The primary outcome was change in the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) after treatment; adverse events were secondary outcomes. Effects were expressed as mean differences (MD) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to rank interventions.
RESULTS: Eleven studies (1,359 patients) were included, evaluating seven strategies: intravenous methylprednisolone (IVMP), intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), IVMP+IVIG, IVMP+plasma exchange (PE), IVMP+IVIG+PE, IVMP+immunoadsorption (IA), and IVMP+efgartigimod (EFG). For efficacy, IVMP+EFG ranked highest in mRS improvement among the included regimens (MD = -0.99, 95% CrI -1.30 to -0.68; SUCRA = 95%), followed by IVMP+IA (MD = -0.87; SUCRA = 88%). IVMP+PE ranked lowest (MD = 0.32; SUCRA = 0.2%). For safety, IVIG monotherapy had the lowest adverse-event risk (RR = 0.51, 95% CrI 0.24 to 0.97), whereas IVMP+PE had the highest risk (RR = 3.10, 95% CrI 0.92 to 9.60).
CONCLUSION: Acute-phase immunotherapy for AE should be individualized by disease severity and antibody subtype. Consistent directional findings were observed in the anti-NMDAR subgroup and, separately, in the subgroup with baseline mRS ≥3. IVMP+EFG and IVMP+IA ranked favorably for short-term functional improvement, although the evidence was based mainly on observational studies and small sample sizes. IVIG remained a reasonable option given its favorable safety profile.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251085606, identifier CRD420251085606.

title: Dual therapy with tofacitinib and steroids for acute severe ulcerative colitis: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: One-third of patients with acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) fail intravenous corticosteroids. We evaluated whether adding tofacitinib to corticosteroids reduces treatment failure in ASUC.
METHODS: In this single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adults with ASUC were randomized 1:1 to tofacitinib (10 mg three times daily for 3 days, then twice daily) or placebo for 5 days alongside corticosteroids. Primary outcome was treatment failure at day 6 (<3-point Lichtiger reduction or total score ≥10, or colectomy). Secondary outcomes were relapse (≥3-point rise with total ≥10), rescue therapy, and colectomy at 90 days. Modified intention-to-treat analysis was performed. (CTRI/2022/11/047186).
RESULTS: Of 62 randomized patients, 58 were analyzed: 33 in the tofacitinib arm and 25 in the placebo arm. The trial was terminated early because of slow recruitment and did not reach the planned sample size of 98. Day 6 treatment failure was numerically lower with tofacitinib in unadjusted analysis (24.2% vs 36.0%; RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.30-1.51; P = .33) and significantly lower after adjustment for baseline covariate imbalance (adjusted RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.24-0.93; P = .03). At 90 days, colectomy rates were similar (12.1% vs 12.0%; P = 1.0), but more tofacitinib-treated patients remained on assigned therapy (84.4% vs 54.2%) and rescue therapy was lower (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.09-0.78; P = .01). Serious adverse events occurred in one versus three patients. No deaths occurred with tofacitinib versus two deaths with placebo.
CONCLUSION: Dual therapy with tofacitinib and steroids in ASUC did not significantly reduce treatment failure at day 6, unless adjustment for baseline imbalance in serum albumin was taken into account. It reduced the need for rescue therapy over 90 days without affecting colectomy risk. Larger clinical trials are required to confirm these findings.

title: Promising therapeutic interventions for preserving endothelial glycocalyx integrity in sepsis: a systematic review.
abstract: Endothelial Glycocalyx (eGCX) degradation is a major pathophysiological event in sepsis, contributing to endothelial dysfunction, vascular permeability, inflammation, microvascular thrombosis, and organ failure. Despite its importance, eGCX-targeted therapies are not currently incorporated into standard sepsis management. This systematic review summarized clinical and preclinical evidence on therapeutic and experimental strategies aimed at preserving or restoring eGCX integrity in sepsis. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched through August 2026. Eligible human and animal studies evaluated eGCX-directed interventions in sepsis or experimental sepsis models. Outcomes included circulating biomarkers such as syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan, microcirculatory measures including perfused boundary region, and structural assessment by microscopy. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, SYRCLE, and ROBINS-I. Twenty-one studies were included, comprising 17 animal and 4 human studies. Interventions included ascorbic acid, sulodexide, doxycycline, activated protein C, heparin-based therapies, antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin, therapeutic plasma exchange, colivelin, liposomal nanocarriers of preassembled eGCX, and rhamnan sulfate. Several interventions reduced eGCX shedding, improved endothelial barrier or microvascular function, and, in some experimental models, preserved or restored eGCX ultrastructure. Overall, the eGCX represents a promising therapeutic target in sepsis; however, most evidence remains preclinical, and well-designed clinical studies using standardized eGCX outcomes are needed.

title: Immune Thrombocytopenia in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
abstract: BackgroundImmune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired immune-mediated platelet disorder. Most evidence informing its diagnosis and management comes from high-income settings as transferability to low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) may not be possible. We conducted a systematic review to characterise adult ITP in this setting.MethodsWe conducted this systematic review in accordance with PRISMA guidance. Studies reporting adult ITP in LMICs were included if they provided data on epidemiology, infections, first- or second-line treatment, or patient-reported outcomes.ResultsTwenty studies were included in this review. ITP often presented in younger adults than typically reported in high-income settings. Secondary ITP accounted for a substantial proportion of cases. Infectious associations, particularly Helicobacter pylori, hepatitis C virus, and HIV, were important contributors to this. Corticosteroids remained the common first-line therapy but was used for prolonged periods. Limited access to newer agents meant that second-line management frequently relied on azathioprine, dapsone, anti-D or splenectomy. Patient-reported outcome data suggested substantial effects on daily activities, work, emotional wellbeing and treatment burden. Most studies, however, were single-centre observational reports and were judged to be at moderate risk of bias.ConclusionITP in LMICs is shaped by distinct factors. Resource-specific diagnostic and treatment frameworks are needed.

title: Risk of myocardial infarction in adults with gout treated with allopurinol: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: AimsAlthough allopurinol is used for urate-lowering therapy, its effect on myocardial infarction risk remains unclear. This study assessed the association between allopurinol use and myocardial infarction in adults with gout.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PROSPERO registration (CRD420261305257). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 2026. Observational studies of adults with confirmed gout that reported adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for myocardial infarction and separately identifiable allopurinol exposure were included. Pooled estimates were calculated using an inverse-variance random-effects model with the Paule-Mandel estimator. Robustness was assessed through leave-one-out, active-comparator, and Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses.ResultsFour retrospective cohort studies met the revised eligibility criteria. In the primary random-effects analysis, allopurinol use was associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.76-0.94; I2 = 0%). However, the association was not statistically significant after excluding the study contributing the greatest weight (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), when restricted to active comparators (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), or using the Hartung-Knapp adjustment (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-1.00).ConclusionAllopurinol therapy was associated with a modest but significant reduction in myocardial infarction risk in adults with gout.

title: Acute dietary fat formulations shape circulating postprandial extracellular vesicle-associated lipid signatures.
abstract: Humans spend much of the day in the postprandial state, yet how acute dietary fat formulations shape lipid signatures associated with circulating extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fractions remains poorly understood. We conducted a randomized acute crossover pilot trial in apparently healthy adults who consumed fat-free, saturated fatty acid (SFA)-, monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA)-, or MUFA-based meals supplemented with ω3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (MUFA + ω3). Plasma SEC-derived EV-enriched fractions were collected at fasting baseline (B), 2-3 h after meal ingestion (postprandial peak, P), and 5-6 h after ingestion (late postprandial phase, LP), and characterized by electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, bead-based surface-marker profiling, untargeted UHPLC-MS/MS lipidomics, and targeted integration of proteomic markers. The recovered fractions showed vesicle-like morphology, comparable NTA-derived particle size distributions and concentrations, dynamic surface-marker profiles, and broad lipidomic coverage comprising 373 lipid species. Significant within-diet species-level changes were detected only at LP under SFA and MUFA + ω3, involving 45 and 57 lipid species, respectively. Eighteen altered species were shared between both formulations, all of them triacylglycerols (TG), whereas 27 were specific to SFA and 39 to MUFA + ω3. Between-diet analyses revealed persistent differences dominated by TG but also involving glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids, with the strongest divergence between SFA and MUFA + ω3 and greater concordance between MUFA and MUFA + ω3. Integration with plasma biochemistry identified an exploratory TG-centered systemic pattern, while proteomic analyses revealed associations of lipid remodeling with both EV-associated tetraspanins and ApoA/ApoB-related signals. These findings support plasma SEC-derived EV-enriched fractions as a dynamic postprandial molecular interface in which dietary fat quality is reflected through coordinated lipid remodeling across vesicular and apolipoprotein-related features.

title: Thermal inactivation kinetics of foodborne viruses across food matrices: a Bayesian meta-analysis and predictive framework.
abstract: Human norovirus and hepatitis A virus are leading causes of foodborne illness, yet their thermal resistance across foods remains difficult to predict. We conducted a Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of time-series thermal inactivation data from 29 studies identified following PRISMA guidelines to quantify the effects of food matrix, virus group, and measurement method. Data from simple buffers, molluscan shellfish, dairy products, berries, and vegetables were evaluated for human enteric viruses and cultivable surrogates. Infectivity- and RT-qPCR-based measurements were analyzed separately to distinguish infectivity loss from loss of detectable genome signal. A Weibull primary inactivation model combined with a log-linear secondary temperature model had the best predictive performance for both outcomes. Food matrix was the strongest predictor of infectivity-based thermal resistance. Molluscan shellfish provided the greatest protection, with a D60°C of 4.30 min [95% CrI: 1.86, 10.79] and a z-value of 30.10 °C [23.14, 42.04], whereas berries had the lowest z-value, 8.92 °C [8.17, 9.79]. Virus groups showed similar thermal behavior after accounting for matrix effects. In RT-qPCR data, genome signal declined slowly during heating, yielding a high global D60°C estimate that varied little across predictors; however, z-values varied by pretreatment, matrix, and virus group. Viability pretreatments improved agreement between RT-qPCR- and infectivity-based estimates, with porcine gastric mucin providing the closest alignment. This Bayesian framework supports the prediction of enteric virus reduction across food-processing conditions to inform evidence-based food safety decisions.

title: Altered GABAB receptor sensitivity in heavy drinkers indexed using a TMS-based biomarker: a randomized controlled experimental medicine trial.
abstract: Metabotropic γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptors (GABABRs) are implicated in alcohol use disorder (AUD) and represent a promising therapeutic target. However, robust biomarkers of GABABRs target engagement and sensitivity in humans are lacking. We examined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-derived cortical inhibition and growth hormone (GH) release as measures of GABABR function, and whether heavy alcohol use is associated with altered responses to pharmacological GABABR activation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 31 healthy volunteers (16 heavy drinkers, 15 light drinkers) received baclofen 30 mg, baclofen 60 mg, or placebo across three sessions. Long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI), short-interval intracortical inhibition, and intracortical facilitation were assessed with paired-pulse TMS at baseline and ~60 min post-dose. Baclofen blood concentrations and plasma GH levels were measured. Baclofen produced dose-dependent increases in GH release, confirming neuroendocrine GABABR engagement. The LICI response to baclofen differed between groups: In light drinkers, baclofen at 30 mg potentiated LICI, and a similar potentiation was seen at 60 mg, indicating that a plateau may have been reached. In contrast, in heavy drinkers, a potentiation of LICI similar to that in light drinkers was seen at 30 mg baclofen, but was absent at the 60 mg dose despite comparable pharmacokinetics, suggesting altered GABABR function. Effects were selective for GABABR-mediated inhibition, with no consistent modulation of short-interval intracortical inhibition or corticospinal excitability. Acute baclofen administration reveals altered GABABR sensitivity in heavy drinkers, with preserved responses at lower doses but reduced response under stronger agonist stimulation. LICI and GH release provide complementary biomarkers of central and peripheral GABABRs engagement and may support translational development of mechanism-based treatments for AUD.

title: Firstline treatment with ruxolitinib versus best available therapy in patients with polycythemia vera: results from the randomized RuxoBEAT trial.
abstract: Ruxolitinib (RUX) is approved as second-line treatment for HU-intolerant/-resistant patients with polycythemia vera (PV). Here, we assessed RUX vs. best available therapy (BAT) as first-line treatment in PV in the randomized multicenter RuxoBEAT clinical trial (NCT02577926). Crossover from BAT to RUX was possible after 6 months. Baseline characteristics in the RUX (n = 44) and BAT (n = 34) arms were comparable. The primary endpoint, the clinico-hematologic complete response (CR) rate at month 6, was not met (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 1.000). Analyses of secondary and exploratory endpoints showed that RUX was significantly more effective than BAT in improving hematocrit, splenomegaly, and patient-reported pruritus and fatigue, but less effective in reducing platelet counts. Compared to baseline, JAK2V617F variant allele frequency decreased significantly in both RUX and BAT groups at 6 months. The time on treatment (p < 0.001) and duration of treatment (p = 0.022) were significantly superior for RUX vs. BAT during the 24-month study period. There were no new safety signals. These findings demonstrate that RUX did not lead to higher CR rates than BAT and suggest that RUX may induce clinically meaningful additional disease improvements in first-line therapy of PV patients.

title: Treatment interventions for co-occurring opioid use disorder, and sleep disturbances: a scoping review.
journal: Substance abuse treatment, prevention, and policy
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is part of the broader spectrum of substance use disorders often complicated by psychiatric symptoms such as depression, anxiety, PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder), and sleep disturbances, with insomnia being particularly frequent. These psychiatric symptoms may act as precipitating factors and consequences of OUD, reinforcing a complex bidirectional relationship that complicates treatment and recovery. Despite the clinical importance of dual disorders, sleep impairments are particularly relevant yet understudied therapeutic targets and literature addressing sleep disturbances in the context of psychiatric symptoms or disorders in OUD remains limited. This scoping review examines pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions of OUD and sleep disturbances in the presence of psychiatric disorders or symptoms, such as anxiety, depression, and PTSD.
METHODS: This review follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines using the following keywords: ("sleep" OR "insomnia") AND ("depression" OR "anxiety" OR "PTSD" OR "post-traumatic stress disorder" OR "posttraumatic stress disorder") AND ("opioid use disorder" OR "OUD" OR "opioid addiction. Sleep disordered breathing was excluded. Participants were adults (> 18 years old) with OUD or opioid dependence undergoing withdrawal or treatment. The study focused on quantitative and qualitative study designs.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies including 1,167 adults with OUD or opioid dependence were selected and categorized into pharmacological (targeting opioid or non-opioid receptors) and non-pharmacological interventions. Most interventions were adjunctive to opioid substitution or antagonist therapies. Naltrexone-induced insomnia was common but did not significantly affect mood and could be mitigated with lorazepam. Non-opioid pharmacotherapies yielded mixed results: guanfacine is suggested to increase insomnia risk but reduce stress and craving, while amitriptyline, prazepam, dronabinol, and neurotransmitter-precursor-supplements showed potential in improving sleep and withdrawal symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: Improved characterization and management of impaired sleep in individuals with OUD and psychiatric symptoms may reduce relapse risk, enhance emotional regulation, and decrease self-medication. Clinicians should consider the complex interplay between OUD, psychiatric symptoms, and sleep as part of comprehensive care. Further research is needed to clarify these interactions and support the development of integrated, evidence-based strategies for treatment and prevention.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: Skeletal effects of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain unclear. This systematic review of eight randomized controlled trials (n = 493) evaluating dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived bone mineral density reports findings separately for each agent, without pooling, because the trials evaluated four pharmacologically distinct agents differing markedly in weight-lowering potency. The evidence is sparse for every agent and is insufficient to establish the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in this population.
PURPOSE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed the randomized evidence on bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers in adults with overweight or obesity, reporting findings separately for each individual agent.
METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review (INPLASY202630076) searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (January 2015 to July 2026). Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with mean baseline body mass index (BMI) > 25 kg/m², compared a GLP-1 RA with placebo or another antidiabetic therapy for ≥12 weeks, and reported BMD assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Because the included trials evaluated pharmacologically distinct agents that differ substantially in weight-lowering potency, results were synthesized narratively and reported separately by agent; no meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Eight RCTs (n = 493) were included. Three trials were at low risk of bias (Eriksson 2019; Hygum 2020; Hansen 2024) and five raised some concerns, principally regarding the randomization process and selective reporting; no agent is supported by more than one trial at low risk of bias. (Cai 2021 contributes two treatment arms assessed separately, giving nine comparisons in the risk-of-bias assessment.) Evidence was unevenly distributed across agents: semaglutide and dulaglutide were each evaluated in one trial, liraglutide in two, and exenatide in five. Five of the eight trials enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes, including all four that randomized an insulin comparator arm; three enrolled adults without diabetes, of which one was defined by obesity alone. By study-level mean baseline BMI, five trials lay in the obese range ( ≥ 30 kg/m²) and three in the overweight range (25 to <30 kg/m²). The single semaglutide trial (Hansen 2024; n = 64; low risk of bias), which produced the largest weight loss of any trial (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -6.8 kg vs placebo), reported reduced lumbar spine BMD (ETD - 0.018 g/cm², p = 0.007), reduced whole-body BMD (mean difference [MD] -0.02 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.03 to -0.01), and increased C-terminal telopeptide (CTX; MD 166.50 pg/mL; 95% CI 66.60 to 266.40). Liraglutide was evaluated at two doses with divergent results. At the weight-management dose of 3.0 mg daily, in the only trial conducted in adults with obesity and without diabetes (Jensen 2024; ETD - 6.7 kg vs placebo), lumbar spine BMD (MD - 0.019 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.034 to -0.004) and total hip BMD (MD - 0.013 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.024 to -0.002) were reduced. At the diabetes dose of 1.8 mg daily (Hygum 2020; -3.8 kg), no site changed materially (lumbar spine MD 0.00 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.01). Exenatide trials were inconsistent, ranging from 0.03 g/cm² (95% CI 0.02 to 0.03) at the lumbar spine (Renyuan 2015) to -0.04 g/cm² (95% CI - 0.15 to 0.07; Akyay 2023). Certainty of evidence was very low for every agent.
CONCLUSION: The randomized evidence is too sparse and too clinically heterogeneous to determine the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity. Each agent has been evaluated in at most five small trials, most conducted in adults with type 2 diabetes rather than in adults with obesity alone. The two trials producing the largest weight loss, one of semaglutide and one of liraglutide 3.0 mg, both reported reduced lumbar spine and total hip BMD at closely similar magnitudes of weight loss, and the semaglutide trial additionally reported increased bone resorption. This convergence warrants dedicated evaluation rather than extrapolation across the drug class. Adequately powered, agent-specific trials with fracture endpoints are required.
PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: INPLASY202630076.

title: Steady-State Pharmacokinetic Drug-Drug Interaction Study of Zastaprazan, a Novel Potassium-Competitive Acid Blocker, and Atorvastatin in Healthy Participants.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Zastaprazan is a novel potassium-competitive acid blocker with CYP3A-mediated metabolism, whereas atorvastatin undergoes CYP3A4- and transporter-mediated disposition. Because these drugs may be co-administered and their net interaction cannot be inferred from shared metabolic pathways alone, this study evaluated their steady-state pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: This open-label, fixed-sequence, three-period, multiple-dose study included healthy Korean men. Participants received atorvastatin 40 mg once daily, zastaprazan 20 mg once daily, and concomitant atorvastatin and zastaprazan, each for 5 consecutive days, under steady-state conditions. Plasma concentrations of zastaprazan, atorvastatin, and 2-hydroxyatorvastatin were measured, and geometric mean ratios (GMRs) with 90% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for C max,ss and AUC τ,ss.
RESULTS: Twenty-four healthy Korean men received at least one dose of a study drug, and 22 were included in the pharmacokinetic analysis. Atorvastatin decreased zastaprazan C max,ss by approximately 26% (GMR, 0.740; 90% CI, 0.655-0.836), whereas AUC τ,ss was preserved (GMR, 1.054; 90% CI, 0.927-1.198). Zastaprazan did not meaningfully alter atorvastatin exposure (C max,ss GMR, 0.982; 90% CI, 0.806-1.195; AUC τ,ss GMR, 1.029; 90% CI, 0.944-1.122). The AUC τ,ss of 2-hydroxyatorvastatin showed a modest decrease (GMR, 0.940; 90% CI, 0.889-0.994) that remained within the predefined conventional reference range. Co-administration was generally well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or adverse event-related discontinuations.
CONCLUSION: Zastaprazan did not meaningfully alter atorvastatin C max,ss or AUC τ,ss under the studied conditions. Although atorvastatin reduced zastaprazan C max,ss, total exposure was preserved, a pattern consistent with altered absorption kinetics without establishing a specific mechanism. The pharmacodynamic significance of the lower zastaprazan C max,ss remains uncertain because intragastric pH was not measured. These pharmacokinetic findings do not suggest a need for atorvastatin dose adjustment under the studied conditions.

title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
abstract: The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.

title: Outcomes of methylprednisolone as an adjunct to endovascular therapy in patients with diabetes and admission hyperglycemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of methylprednisolone as adjunctive treatment to endovascular therapy (EVT) in patients with and without diabetes, as well as in patients with and without admission hyperglycemia.
METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the MARVEL trial. The primary outcome was the ordinal modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included mRS score of 0-3, 0-2, 0-1 at 90 days. Safety outcomes included mortality within 90 days, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) and any ICH within 48 hours.
RESULTS: Among 1,678 patients from the MARVEL trial, 321 had history of diabetes. In patients with diabetes, methylprednisolone was not associated with improved 90-day mRS [common odds radio (cOR), 1.07 (0.81-1.40), P = 0.640] but was associated with more any ICH within 48 hours [OR, 1.63 (1.17-2.26), P = 0.004]. In patients without diabetes, methylprednisolone was associated with better 90-day mRS [cOR, 1.16 (1.02-1.33), P = 0.026] and lower 90-day mortality [OR, 0.74 (0.62-0.88), P = 0.001]. A significant treatment-by-diabetes-history interaction was observed only for any ICH within 48 hours (P for interaction = 0.036). Among 1,470 patients stratified by admission hyperglycemia, methylprednisolone was not associated with improved 90-day mRS in either subgroup.
CONCLUSION: The glycemia status-by-treatment interaction was not significant. A benefit trend was observed with adjunctive methylprednisolone in patients without diabetes. However, adjunctive use of methylprednisolone in patients with diabetes may be with a higher risk of any intracranial hemorrhage. Admission hyperglycemia status did not significantly modify the effectiveness or safety of methylprednisolone. These findings warrant validation in further studies.

title: Atosiban versus nifedipine for the management of preterm labor: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy, maternal safety, and neonatal outcomes of atosiban versus nifedipine in the management of preterm labor, with particular attention to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rates.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, EBSCOHost, ClinicalTrials.gov and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were systematically searched up to May 25, 2025. No language restrictions were applied.
STUDY SELECTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing atosiban and nifedipine in women with clinically diagnosed preterm labor were included, provided they reported at least one outcome related to pregnancy prolongation. Six RCTs comprising 1,070 patients met inclusion criteria.
DATA COLLECTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data on efficacy, maternal adverse effects, and neonatal outcomes using a standardized form. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Pooled analyses showed no significant difference between atosiban and nifedipine in delaying delivery for 48 hours (risk ratio [RR] 1.09; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.23) or 7 days (RR 1.04; 95% CI 0.89-1.22). Atosiban was associated with a significantly lower risk of maternal headache, hypotension, and tachycardia. Atosiban was associated with a non-statistically significant trend toward higher NICU admission (RR 1.36; 95% CI 0.97-1.94; p=0.079), an estimate derived from only two RCTs with substantial heterogeneity (I2=69.8%) and warranting cautious interpretation. No significant differences were observed for neonatal death, sepsis, or hemorrhagic disease.
CONCLUSION: Atosiban and nifedipine offer comparable tocolytic efficacy. Atosiban carries a more favorable maternal safety profile but shows a non-significant trend toward higher NICU admission warranting confirmation in larger trials. Tocolytic selection should therefore be individualized, weighing maternal tolerability against this uncertain neonatal signal.Systematic Review Registration: PROSPERO CRD420251065426.

title: Hematological and biochemical responses to three doses of caffeine during the CrossFit® workout: a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigated the effects of three doses of caffeine (CAF) on hematological and biochemical responses during the CrossFit® workout, a protocol known to induce significant physiological fluctuations.
METHODS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo (PLA)-controlled crossover trial, 26 moderately trained CrossFit® athletes received acute doses of 3, 6, or 9 mgCAF/kgbody mass (BM), or a PLA, 70 min before a 17-min CrossFit® workout.
RESULTS: While exercise was the predominant driver of hematological changes, with no CAF-specific modulation of blood cell indices, significant treatment × time point interactions were observed solely for glucose concentration. Specifically, MEDIUM (6 mgCAF/kgBM) and HIGH (9 mgCAF/kgBM) CAF doses produced significantly greater post-exercise glucose elevations compared to baseline and PLA visits. Phosphates concentrations increased over time, particularly post-exercise, with no treatment effect retained after excluding baseline visit in the sensitivity analysis. Calcium level dynamics were influenced by temporal factors rather than CAF, and magnesium concentration remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that acute CAF ingestion selectively influences post-exercise glucose responses during the CrossFit® workout, whereas hematological variables and most biochemical markers remain unaffected. Significant post-exercise glucose elevations were observed following the 6 and 9 mgCAF/kgBM conditions compared with baseline and PLA visits, while serum mineral concentrations remained largely stable across treatments.

title: Management of shift work disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine systematic review, meta-analysis, and GRADE assessment.
journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The purpose of this systematic review is to provide supporting evidence for a clinical practice guideline on the treatment of adults with shift work disorder (SWD).
METHODS: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine commissioned a task force of six experts in sleep and circadian medicine. A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and treatment trials in which treatments for the symptoms of excessive sleepiness and/or sleep disturbance/insomnia in adults with SWD, and for circadian adaptation to shift work schedules was tested. Evidence from controlled laboratory trials of simulated shift work and of field-based trials of shift workers with and without a diagnosis of SWD was included. Statistical analyses were performed to determine the significance of critical and important outcomes and clinically meaningful thresholds were set to determine the clinical relevance of treatments on the outcomes examined, where possible. Finally, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) process was used to assess the evidence for making recommendations.
RESULTS: The literature search resulted in 3,045 articles; 118 studies provided data suitable for statistical analyses. The task force provided a detailed summary of the evidence along with the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, and resource use considerations.

title: Effectiveness and safety of atorvastatin/ ezetimibe fixed-dose combination in hypercholesterolemia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients fail to achieve low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets with statin monotherapy, calling for a combination of statins and ezetimibe. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the comparative effectiveness and safety of atorvastatin monotherapy, atorvastatin/ezetimibe free-equivalent combination (AS/EZ FEC), and fixed-dose combination (AS/EZ FDC) in patients with hypercholesterolemia.
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials were retrieved from electronic databases. Primary outcomes were the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline and LDL-C goal attainment, analyzed using mean difference (MD) and risk ratio (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Treatments were ranked via surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). The two combination therapies were compared to AS alone for their safety profiles and tolerability. Forty-six trials (n = 10,567) were included.
RESULTS: AS/EZ FDC reduced LDL-C more than AS alone (MD -13.94%, 95% CI [-18.90% to -9.10%]), with similar results for AS/EZ FEC (MD -12.41%, 95% CI [-14.61% to -10.22%]). SUCRA rankings for LDL-C reduction were FDC (86.2%), FEC (63.8%), and AS (0.0%). For LDL-C goal attainment, the RR was 1.87 (95% CI [1.47-2.39]) for FEC vs. monotherapy, 1.80 (95% CI [0.85-3.81]) for FDC vs. monotherapy. No significant differences in safety profiles were observed between treatments.
CONCLUSION: AS/EZ combination therapies provide greater improvements in LDL-C reduction and goal attainment compared with AS monotherapy, with FDC ranking highest in LDL-C reduction. Treatment with AS/EZ FEC or FDC did not increase the risk of adverse events compared to AS monotherapy and was well tolerated. These findings support FDC use when intensive LDL-C lowering is required.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure.
RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.

title: Marine-Derived Functional Foods for Host-Directed Tuberculosis Therapy: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Host-Pathogen Crosstalk.
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a global health challenge, motivating research into marine-derived compounds as potential host-directed adjuncts. This systematic review synthesized seven eligible experimental studies identified through a semantic literature search, evaluating omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), fucoxanthin, caulerpin, and fucoidan. Findings were synthesized narratively because methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. No included study directly evaluated marine-derived peptides or peptide hydrolysates. Caulerpin reduced intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis burden, but its NLRP3 and cytokine effects were examined in a non-tuberculous mycobacterial model. Fucoxanthin-containing fractions demonstrated direct antimycobacterial activity and reduced organ bacterial burden without establishing a causal host-directed pathway in TB. Fucoidan microparticles supported drug delivery; growth inhibition was demonstrated for an isoniazid/rifabutin-containing formulation, without establishing an independent fucoidan effect. Omega-3 PUFAs yielded contradictory findings, impairing macrophage antimicrobial activity in vitro while reducing bacterial burden in some animal models. Differences in host species, nutritional status, granuloma pathology, and intervention timing may explain these discrepancies. Marine-derived compounds show preliminary potential, but host-associated outcomes, direct antimicrobial activity, and formulation effects require separate interpretation. Heterogeneous preclinical designs and limited safety evidence constrain translation. Further research should establish TB-specific mechanisms, evaluate safety, and investigate peptides and adjunctive combinations with conventional therapy.

title: Acorus calamus L. for Cognitive Enhancement: A Systematic Review of Its Ethnobotanical Practices and Scientific Evidence.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acorus calamus L. is an important medicinal aromatic plant belonging to Acoraceae family. The current review article underscores the ethnobotanical significance along with scientific evidence on cognitive and neurological properties of A. calamus. Besides these, the article reports the morphology, phytochemistry and biological activities of A. calamus.
METHODS: Using PRISMA (2020) guidelines, an extensive literature review have been searched using PubChem, Google Scholar, Wiley online library, Sci-Hub and ScienceDirect. Using key words such as A. calamus, phytochemistry, ethnobotany, pharmacology, cognitive enhancement information was collected from the above sites.
RESULTS: A. calamus possesses valuable phytochemicals having wide range of biological applications. The essential oil contains high levels of β - asarone, camphene, β ocimene, camphor, calarene, α selinene, and cadinol. Pharmacologically, A. calamus possesses diverse medicinal property including antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-diabetic potential which make the plant more valuable. Previously reported numerous studies related to in vitro, in vivo and in silico results showed the plant possesses significant efficacy on neurological and memory related aspects.
CONCLUSION: The present review covers all the previous studies on neurological aspects as well as cognitive related studies.

title: Challenges of Conducting a Feasibility Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial During COVID-19 Restrictions: Rivaroxaban Versus Acetyl Salicylic Acid in Patients with Multiple Myeloma on Lenalidomide-Based Therapy (RithMM).
abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a serious medical complication with an increased risk in patients with multiple myeloma undergoing combination treatment regimens. Acetylsalicylic acid is routinely used as a method of thromboprophylaxis in multiple myeloma patients treated with lenalidomide, and rivaroxaban has been assessed in small-scale studies in multiple myeloma patients treated with immunomodulatory drugs; yet, no study has compared the two methods. In this pilot, we asked if a full-scale trial would be feasible to assess the benefits of rivaroxaban over acetylsalicylic acid as a thromboprophylactic approach. This pilot recruited patients with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide-based therapy and randomized them to either low-dose acetylsalicylic acid or rivaroxaban, then monitored bleeding and thrombotic events throughout lenalidomide-dexamethasone treatment. A total of 55 patients were recruited across three Canadian centres, with two venous thromboembolic events and two bleeding events, all in the acetylsalicylic acid arm. We conducted a post hoc analysis of active recruitment time as a definition of recruitment feasibility, as we did not achieve our pre-defined feasibility goals. Despite the challenges in enrollment, possibly due to social restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic, we maintain that a full-scale trial is feasible and offers insight into thromboprophylactic management in this population.

title: Therapeutic Potential of Marine Natural Products Against Alzheimer's Disease: Molecular Mechanisms, Druggability Evaluation and Clinical Translation Barriers.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative disorder with complex multifactorial pathological cascades, including amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregation, tau hyperphosphorylation, sustained neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, cholinergic dysfunction and gut-brain axis imbalance. Current marketed anti-AD drugs merely relieve symptomatic cognitive impairment without halting or reversing disease progression, highlighting an urgent demand for novel multi-target therapeutic candidates. Marine ecosystems, covering 71% of the Earth's surface, generate structurally unique, low-toxicity secondary metabolites via adaptive metabolic pathways of marine algae, invertebrates and microorganisms, which represent promising lead compounds for developing marine anti-AD therapeutics with synergistic multitarget neuroprotective activities. This systematic review comprehensively summarizes the anti-AD bioactivities and underlying molecular mechanisms of seven major categories of marine natural products, including marine polysaccharides, terpenoids, macrolides, alkaloids, polyphenols and carotenoids, sterols/lipids, and aminosulfonates. We further perform an integrated ADMET druggability assessment of representative marine bioactive molecules to evaluate their blood-brain barrier penetration, oral absorption, physicochemical properties and toxicological risks, identifying homotaurine as the most balanced candidate with favorable central nervous system delivery and safety profiles. We also elaborate the core bottlenecks restricting clinical translation, including insufficient blood-brain barrier permeability and unsatisfactory in vivo pharmacokinetic behaviors of most marine-derived compounds. Finally, we outline future research directions, covering structural modification, nanocarrier delivery, gut-brain axis-targeted intervention and cross-disciplinary translational research. This work aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical reference for the discovery, optimization and clinical transformation of marine anti-Alzheimer drugs, and facilitate high-value exploitation of marine bioactive resources for neurodegenerative disease treatment.
