title: Comparative Effectiveness of Tricyclic Antidepressants, Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors, and Anticonvulsants for Diabetic Painful Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Introduction: Diabetic painful neuropathy (DPN) is one of the most common and debilitating complications of diabetes, substantially impairing the quality of life of patients. In the absence of disease-modifying therapies, treatment remains focused on symptomatic pain control with non-opioid pharmacologic agents; however, comparative evidence guiding optimal medication selection remains limited. Using a systematic review, pairwise meta-analysis, and network meta-analysis, this study compares the effectiveness of current non-opioid-based treatments, including amitriptyline, duloxetine, gabapentin, and pregabalin, for pain reduction in patients with DPN. Methods: PubMed and Google Scholar were systematically searched for randomized and clinical trials published between 2010 and 2025 evaluating these medications as monotherapy for DPN. A total of n = 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. Pain outcomes measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), Visual Analog Scale (VAS), or Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) were standardized to a common metric. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses were performed to estimate within-drug treatment effects, followed by a frequentist network meta-analysis to compare therapies through direct and indirect evidence. Mean change in pain severity was the primary outcome. We performed heterogeneity, network consistency, and sensitivity analyses under varying correlation assumptions. Results: A total of 1397 participants across 11 studies were included. Pairwise meta-analysis demonstrated substantial pain reduction with duloxetine (mean change [MC] 27.8; 95% CI 18.5-37.1), gabapentin (MC 34.8; 95% CI 9.3-60.3), and pregabalin (MC 19.7; 95% CI 8.9-30.5). Although amitriptyline trials individually reported improvement, the pooled estimate did not reach statistical significance. Network meta-analysis indicated that gabapentin, duloxetine, and amitriptyline were associated with better estimated analgesic benefit than pregabalin; the differences among gabapentin, duloxetine, and amitriptyline were modest and not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings, and no significant network inconsistency was detected. Conclusions: Commonly used non-opioid pharmacologic therapies for DPN provide broadly comparable analgesic benefit, with gabapentin showing comparatively preferable reduction in pain severity within the network analysis. Given the modest differences between agents and substantial variability in individual response, treatment decisions should be individualized according to patient comorbidities, tolerability, and therapeutic goals. Larger, methodologically standardized comparative trials are needed to strengthen the evidence base and support more precise, evidence-based management of DPN.

title: Oteseconazole (VT-1161) for the Management of Dermatophyte Toenail Onychomycosis: A Review of Phase II Trial Subgroup Efficacy and Extended Follow-Up Safety.
abstract: Oteseconazole, a synthetic tetrazole antifungal, provides pharmacological advantages that suggest it can be a safe and effective treatment for Trichophyton rubrum onychomycosis. A Phase II study of oteseconazole (VT-1161) for onychomycosis demonstrated good efficacy and safety up to Week 60 in the dosing regimens tested: 300 mg for 12 weeks; 300 mg for 24 weeks; 600 mg for 12 weeks and 600 mg for 24 weeks (all given once daily for 2 weeks, then once weekly for remaining weeks). Additional analysis of efficacy was performed using patient factors that can impact onychomycosis. Similar efficacy rates were found across all four regimens tested. Patient factors (<50 years of age, <50% affected nail area) were more strongly associated with improved outcomes than dose escalation of oteseconazole but did not necessarily predict better overall outcomes. No significant safety concerns were found up to Week 60. New extended follow-up data from Week 60 to Week 96 demonstrated long-term plasma retention of oteseconazole with no additional oteseconazole-related adverse events. Accordingly, clinical photographic assessment at Weeks 72 and 96 showed improvement in the target toenail; however, the number of evaluable patients was limited (n = 22), and mycology testing was not performed. The tetrazole structure of oteseconazole significantly reduces the risk of drug-drug interaction compared to traditional azoles (itraconazole, fluconazole). The favorable safety and efficacy profile suggests oteseconazole could be a potential alternative to itraconazole for onychomycosis at any of the tested doses.

title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort.
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).
RESULTS: All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, -4.20; 95% CI, -4.53 to -3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period.
CONCLUSIONS: The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004.

title: Treatment with sildenafil oral film improves orgasmic intensity: a secondary, exploratory post-hoc analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Erectile dysfunction (ED) impairs sexual function beyond erection itself, yet its effect on orgasmic intensity, measurable by the validated psychometric tool Orgasmometer, remains largely unexplored. Sildenafil oral film (OF) is a novel formulation offering rapid dissolution and flexible dosing (25-100 mg, including an intermediate 75 mg dose).
AIM: To investigate the relationship between ED severity and orgasmic intensity, and to evaluate whether Sildenafil OF restores orgasmic intensity in men with ED.
METHODS: This secondary, exploratory analysis of orgasmic intensity was not prespecified and was performed post-hoc on a Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, flexible-dose, placebo-controlled trial conducted across 17 US centers (January-December 2024; NCT05490680). Heterosexual men with a ≥6-month ED diagnosis were randomized 3:1 to Sildenafil OF or placebo for 12 weeks. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and at weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12.
OUTCOMES: Primary endpoints were the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF) Erectile Function domain and Sexual Encounter Profile questions 2 and 3 (SEP2/SEP3). The secondary endpoint of interest was the Orgasmometer score, alongside the Erection Hardness Score (EHS) and all IIEF domains.
RESULTS: Of 488 randomized participants, 439 completed all visits (Sildenafil OF: n = 326; placebo: n = 113). Baseline Orgasmometer scores progressively declined with ED severity (P < .001). Sildenafil OF significantly improved Orgasmometer scores versus placebo at week 2 (+1.67, P < .001), with continued improvement through week 12. Linear mixed-effects models identified the composite erectile score (EHS, SEP2, SEP3) as the strongest predictor of orgasmic intensity (β = 1.05 ± 0.03, P < .001). A formal counterfactual mediation analysis showed that erectile improvement partially mediated the treatment effect (indirect effect 0.66, 95% CI, 0.26-1.18; proportion mediated ~43%, 95% CI, 21%-67%), with a significant direct effect persisting (0.86, 95% CI, 0.41-1.37).
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Because erectile improvement explained ~43% of the effect on orgasmic intensity, erectile measures alone may not fully capture treatment response; a single-item assessment of orgasmic intensity may therefore complement erectile evaluation in men with ED. Sildenafil OF represents an effective, patient-friendly option addressing both domains.
STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS: Strengths include large sample size, rigorous randomized controlled trial design, and use of a validated measure. Limitations include restriction to heterosexual men, absence of a healthy control group, and post-hoc analysis.
CONCLUSION: In men with ED, orgasmic intensity was progressively lower with increasing ED severity, and treatment with Sildenafil OF improved it substantially, but not exclusively, through improvements in erectile rigidity and maintenance. Orgasmic intensity is a clinically relevant, low-burden measure that may complement erectile assessment in men with ED.

title: Gut relief revisited: plecanatide in chronic idiopathic constipation and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation - a systematic review and meta-analysis with GRADE assessment.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) are prevalent gastrointestinal disorders with limited effective treatment options. CIC affects approximately 14% of the population worldwide, particularly women, and is marked by difficult defecation, while IBS-C also includes abdominal pain as a core of symptom. Plecanatide, a guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) agonist approved in 2017, has shown promise in improving stool consistency and symptoms; however, its optimal therapeutic dose remains unclear.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted through (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase) for randomized controlled trials comparing plecanatide with placebo until August 2025. Primary outcomes included changes in complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs), spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs), and stool consistency.
RESULTS: Plecanatide significantly increased the changes in complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs) across all reported doses with mean differences (MDs) of (0.75, 0.92, 0.80, and 1.00, (P < 0.00001), with the greatest improvement observed at the 9 mg dose. Moreover, spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs) improved significantly at 1, 3, and 6 mg, with (MDs: 0.97, 1.50, and 1.58, (P < 0.00001). Stool consistency and reduction in abdominal pain and bloating were observed particularly at 3-6 mg. Furthermore, plecanatide demonstrated consistent efficacy across all doses, with both 1 mg and 9 mg showing significantly greater improvements in CSBMs and SBMs compared to the 0.3 mg dose. Diarrhea was the most frequent adverse event and the primary reason for treatment discontinuation, while other safety outcomes were not significantly affected.
CONCLUSION: Plecanatide is generally well-tolerated in the treatment of CIC and IBS-C, with the 3 mg dose, offering the best balance between efficacy and safety. This meta-analysis supports its use as a viable treatment option, though diarrhea remains a dose-related concern.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered prospectively with PROSPERO (Registration number: CRD420251066097, Date of registration: 2025-6-10).

title: Pyrexia of unknown origin (PUO) in South Asia: a systematic review of etiology, diagnostic gaps and management practices.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pyrexia of Unknown Origin (PUO), also referred to as Fever of Unknown Origin (FUO), remains a persistent diagnostic challenge in clinical practice. In South Asian regions, endemic infections, resource constraints, variable diagnostic capacity, and heterogeneous clinical practices may further complicate evaluation. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence on the etiology, diagnostic approaches, reported management practices, and systemic barriers related to PUO in the region to inform improved clinical guidelines and health policies.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in major electronic databases following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251170142). Observational studies and large case series reporting PUO among all populations in South Asian countries were included. Dual independent screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools for observational studies and QUADAS-2 (Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies) for diagnostic accuracy studies. Findings were synthesized narratively due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven studies were included, with infectious diseases predominating, most commonly tuberculosis, enteric fever, and scrub typhus. Non-infectious inflammatory diseases and malignancies accounted for significant minorities. Diagnostic yield varied substantially across studies, with higher yields reported in settings with greater access to advanced diagnostic modalities. Key systemic barriers included limited laboratory and imaging capacity, high rates of empirical antimicrobial use, absence of standardized diagnostic protocols, and patient-related factors like late presentation and cost. Reported management frequently involved empirical use of third-generation cephalosporins and doxycycline. Evidence was geographically imbalanced and India-dominant, with approximately 54% of included studies originating in India and nearly all conducted in tertiary hospital settings.
CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence suggests that PUO in South Asia is heterogeneous, with infections, particularly tuberculosis and other endemic infections, most frequently reported. Findings should be interpreted cautiously because studies were dominated by Indian tertiary-care settings and varied in definitions, diagnostic capacity, and confirmation criteria. Future research should prioritize standardized PUO definitions, transparent diagnostic-confirmation categories, prospective multicenter studies in underrepresented settings, and validated resource-stratified diagnostic pathways. Pragmatic early referral thresholds, such as persistent fever for 7-14 days without diagnosis after initial evaluation, may be explored in low-resource settings but require prospective validation.

title: Prenatal antiseizure medication exposure and offspring structural and neurodevelopmental outcomes: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Review-level evidence on prenatal antiseizure medication (ASM) exposure is difficult to interpret because outcome domains are often synthesized separately, primary studies overlap, and comparator frameworks and certainty vary. We aimed to calibrate evidence across structural and neurodevelopmental outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted an anchor-based umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PROSPERO: CRD420251142541), searching four databases through December 31, 2025. One prespecified anchor review represented each drug-outcome-comparator question; overlapping reviews were not combined into second-order pooled estimates. AMSTAR 2, corrected covered area, GRADE, and directional umbrella-credibility classes were applied, with NS assigned when the 95% confidence interval included the null.
RESULTS: Fourteen reviews were included: nine structural and five neurodevelopmental. All had Low or Critically Low AMSTAR 2 confidence, and ASD/ADHD review overlap was very high (CCA, 28.1%). Valproate showed the most consistent retained pattern, including Class I credibility for combined major congenital anomalies and the most credible retained neurodevelopmental signal for autism spectrum disorder (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.10; 95% CI, 2.24-4.28; Low certainty; Class II). Topiramate showed an oral-cleft signal with Low certainty and Class III credibility. The lamotrigine estimate for major congenital anomalies was NS, whereas the orofacial-cleft estimate excluded the null but had Very Low certainty (OR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.05-1.92; Class IV). Other retained neurodevelopmental anchors had Very Low certainty and were Class IV or NS; no independent pairwise neurodevelopmental anchor was available for carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, or levetiracetam.
CONCLUSIONS: Review-level evidence was most consistent for valproate and aligned with its established structural and neurodevelopmental risks. NS or Very Low-certainty findings for non-valproate ASMs should not be interpreted as evidence of no risk. Comparative safety requires individualized risk-benefit assessment rather than binary safety classifications.

title: Efficacy of fosfomycin tromethamine powder in preventing biofilm-forming bacterial colonization on double-j stents in patients with upper urinary tract calculi.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of fosfomycin tromethamine powder (FMT) for preventing biofilm-forming bacterial colonization on double-J (DJ) stents in patients with upper urinary tract calculi.
METHODS: From January 2024 to June 2025, we prospectively enrolled 200 adult patients with upper urinary tract calculi undergoing double-J stent placement after endoscopic laser lithotripsy at our tertiary medical center and randomly assigned them in a 1:1 ratio to the experimental or control group (n = 100 per group). Patients in the experimental group received a single oral dose of 3 g FMT one day before double-J stent placement and on postoperative days 7 and 15. Patients in the control group received intravenous cefuroxime (CXM), 1.5 g per dose, administered twice daily one day before stent placement and on postoperative days 1 and 2. Stent surface samples were collected at the time of DJ stent removal for quantitative bacterial biofilm culture, microbial species identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Baseline clinical characteristics, Double-J Stent Symptom Score (DJSS) (assessed during indwelling), SF-36 Health Survey quality-of-life score, numerical rating scale (NRS) pain score, and urine analysis parameters at stent removal were systematically recorded. All statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS version 26.0, with statistical significance defined as a two-sided p-value < 0.05.
RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the experimental and control groups. Biofilm-forming bacterial colonization was identified in 49 individuals (24.5%). The colonization rate was significantly lower in the experimental group (17/100, 17%) than in the control group (32/100, 32%) (χ² = 6.082, P = 0.014). The experimental group demonstrated statistically significant improvements over the control group in preventing ureteral stent syndrome, reducing postoperative pyrexia incidence, decreasing urine leukocyte esterase positivity rate, lowering urinary leukocyte count, alleviating postoperative pain (assessed using a numerical rating scale), and improving SF-36 health survey quality-of-life scores (all P < 0.05). The three most frequently isolated pathogens were Escherichia coli (E. coli) (n = 17, 34.7%), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 8, 16.3%), and Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 5, 10.2%). Antimicrobial susceptibility testing demonstrated that Gram-negative bacilli exhibited high-level resistance to ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, cefazolin, cefuroxime, and ceftriaxone. In contrast, these isolates remained highly susceptible to β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations (cefoperazone/sulbactam and piperacillin/tazobactam), carbapenems (meropenem, imipenem, and ertapenem), cefotetan, nitrofurantoin, and fosfomycin. Gram-positive cocci exhibited high-level resistance to oxacillin, penicillin G, cefoxitin, and erythromycin. Conversely, these isolates demonstrated consistently high susceptibility to linezolid, vancomycin, tigecycline, and rifampicin. Fungal isolates showed high susceptibility to itraconazole, fluconazole, voriconazole, 5-fluorouracil, and amphotericin B.
CONCLUSION: When both groups received a fixed 3-day drug regimen, Compared to CXM, FMT may reduce the proportion of upper urinary tract calculi patients with biofilm-forming bacteria on DJ stents in this region. These findings support FMT-rather than CXM-as the preferred agent for targeted prophylaxis in this region-specific patient population and underscore the importance of rational antibiotic use. Optimizing infection prevention strategies requires integration of antimicrobial susceptibility test results with population-specific clinical characteristics, including established infection risk factors.

title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires effective sedation to ensure patient comfort while preserving gas exchange, hemodynamic stability, and predictable recovery. Remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to traditional sedatives. However, its safety and efficacy compared with those of other sedatives remain under investigation. This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of remimazolam versus dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol in adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy.
METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted using 5 databases through January 2026. Outcomes included respiratory depression, hypotension, bradycardia, time to target sedation depth, procedure success rate, emergence time, and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Relative risks (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2325 patients) were included. Remimazolam significantly reduced respiratory depression (RR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.36-0.73, P<0.001), hypotension (RR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.34-0.73, P<0.001), and bradycardia (RR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.65, P=0.001) versus controls. Sedation onset was faster than dexmedetomidine (MD: -2.19 min), but slower than propofol (MD: 0.49 min). Success rates were comparable across groups (RR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.98-1.28, P=0.097). Compared with dexmedetomidine and midazolam, remimazolam shortened emergence (MD: -1.79 and -4.37 min, respectively) and PACU stay (MD: -3.58 and -6.70 min).
CONCLUSION: Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Ushaq Capsule as Adjunctive Therapy in Patients With Lumbar Radiculopathy: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial at Imam Khomeini Hospital, Tehran, Iran.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sciatica and lumbar radicular pain are prevalent symptoms affecting a large proportion of people worldwide. Many patients seek complementary and alternative medicine for pain relief. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Ushaq capsule, a herbal formulation from Traditional Persian Medicine, on pain intensity and disability in patients with lumbar radiculopathy.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial included 68 patients randomly assigned to intervention or placebo groups. All participants were allowed to use diclofenac 50 mg (up to three tablets daily) as rescue medication for breakthrough pain. Participants in the intervention group received 3 Ushaq capsules daily for 6 weeks, while the placebo group received identical microcrystalline cellulose capsules. Pain intensity and disability were assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ). The primary endpoint was the change in VAS score from baseline to week 6. Safety was evaluated through clinical adverse event monitoring and laboratory tests.
RESULTS: No significant baseline differences were observed between the groups (p > 0.05). The mean VAS score was significantly lower in the Ushaq group from the second week onward (p = 0.019) and remained significant until the end of the study (p = 0.003). The RMDQ score decreased significantly in both groups, but the reduction in the Ushaq group was not significantly greater than that in the placebo group (p = 0.218). No serious adverse events were reported; only mild, transient gastrointestinal discomfort occurred (Ushaq: 6.5%, placebo: 4.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: Ushaq capsules as adjunctive therapy with diclofenac as rescue medication showed greater pain reduction compared to placebo with a favourable safety profile. Larger, longer-term trials with active comparators are needed to confirm these preliminary findings.
TRAIL REGISTRATION: The research was registered with the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT) and received registration number IRCT20200418047124N1.

title: Effect of a potassium-competitive acid blocker on the gut microbiota in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomized pilot study.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are routinely used in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to prevent gastrointestinal bleeding associated with dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). However, long-term PPI use has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis. Tegoprazan, a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), may exert distinct effects on the gut microbiome. This study compared the longitudinal effects of tegoprazan and pantoprazole on gut microbiota composition in patients with angina undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study randomized 38 patients 1:1:1 to tegoprazan 50 mg once daily, pantoprazole 40 mg once daily, or no acid-suppressive therapy for 24 weeks. Five participants did not provide baseline fecal samples, and nine discontinued participation before week 24. Thus, 24 participants with paired baseline and week-24 fecal samples were included in the final analysis. Fecal samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
RESULTS: No drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in any group. Observed amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness was significantly higher at week 24 than at baseline in the overall cohort (p = 0.003) and P-CAB group (p = 0.016), whereas the Shannon index showed no significant changes. Paired PERMANOVA with permutations restricted by patient ID revealed significant differences in Bray-Curtis beta diversity between baseline and week 24 in the P-CAB group (R² = 0.070, p = 0.031) and PPI group (R² = 0.059, p = 0.008), but not in the no acid-suppressive therapy group (R² = 0.021, p = 0.691). In the formal cross-arm analysis, the treatment group-by-visit interaction was not significant for Bray-Curtis beta diversity (R² = 0.021, pseudo-F = 0.505, p = 0.270). Although nominal within-arm taxonomic changes were observed, no treatment group-by-visit interaction survived Benjamini-Hochberg correction in ANCOM-BC2.
CONCLUSION: Tegoprazan was well tolerated, with no drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding during the 24-week follow-up. Both acid-suppressive treatment groups showed modest longitudinal microbiome changes. The taxon-level findings were exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of treatment-specific differential effects. Larger, adequately powered studies are required to confirm these observations.

title: Dried blood spot IP-10 as a biomarker of tuberculosis severity and treatment responses: results from a phase IIb trial of adjunctive acetylsalicylic acid and ibuprofen.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Host-directed therapies may improve tuberculosis (TB) outcomes by modulating immune responses and attenuating hyperinflammation, yet accessible biomarkers remain limited. We hypothesized that interferon-γ-inducible protein 10 (IP-10/CXCL10) measured in dried blood spot (DBS), a low-threshold and field-adapted sampling method, has potential as a biomarker for treatment response in pulmonary TB. Accordingly, we assessed IP-10 levels in patients receiving adjunctive acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) or ibuprofen (IBU) alongside TB standard therapy.
METHODS: IP-10 levels were quantified longitudinally in DBS from 120 pulmonary TB patients enrolled in the SMA-TB clinical trial (NCT04575519) at two sites in South Africa. Samples collected at baseline, week 2, week 8, and week 24 were analyzed by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Associations with disease severity and treatment response were assessed, and the predictive value of IP-10 for microbiological, clinical, and radiological outcomes was evaluated.
RESULTS: IP-10 levels correlated with TB disease severity, with higher concentrations observed in patients with elevated clinical and radiological scores and positive sputum acid-fast-bacilli staining. This association was reflected in treatment response, as patients with good clinical outcomes exhibited an earlier decline in IP-10 (week 8, p=0.0005), whereas those with poor outcomes showed a delayed decline (week 24, p<0.0001). Overall, IP-10 levels decreased during treatment irrespective of intervention or HIV status, with no significant differences between treatment arms at week 24. Notably, IP-10 levels at week 2 predicted rapid sputum culture conversion in the IBU arm, as well as in HIV-negative patients in the ASA arm (AUC: ASA 0.79; IBU 0.76).
CONCLUSION: IP-10 levels measured in DBS are associated with disease severity and treatment response and may serve as a biomarker for therapy monitoring and early prediction of microbiological outcomes in TB, irrespective of adjunctive host-directed therapies. These findings require validation in larger patient cohorts before the method can be implemented in clinical practice.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy in Patients with Cancer: A Review of Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for the management of obesity and type 2 diabetes, including among patients with cancer. Although previous research has mainly focused on cancer incidence, their associations with clinical outcomes after cancer diagnosis remain less well characterized. Therefore, the present study aimed to evaluate the oncologic and survival outcomes associated with GLP-1 RA use in adults with an established malignancy. We performed a systematic review of comparative studies evaluating GLP-1 RA use in patients with a confirmed cancer diagnosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications from 1 January 2016 to 8 August 2026. Twenty-six retrospective cohort studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Thirteen studies included selective GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide within the same exposure group. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Twenty-five studies evaluated overall survival and/or all-cause mortality, while nine assessed cancer recurrence, progression, or related outcomes. Survival and mortality outcomes more often favored the exposed group (especially compared with nonuse) than not, but findings were less consistent in active-comparator analyses. Evidence for recurrence and progression was sparse and heterogeneous, and no clear signal of increased risk was observed. Because all of these were observational studies with substantial differences in populations, comparators, exposure definitions, and duration of follow-up, the survival associations do not imply causality or direct antitumor effects of GLP-1 RAs. Clinically, the preponderance of evidence does not support the use of GLP-1 RAs as cancer-directed therapy, and their use in patients with cancer should be guided by established indications such as obesity and type 2 diabetes. Potential explanations include effects on glycemic and cardiovascular risk factors, treatment selection, residual confounding, or combinations thereof. Prospective studies and randomized controlled trials with cancer-specific outcomes and longer follow-up are needed to further evaluate these associations.

title: Efficacy and safety of Lianhua Qingwen versus oseltamivir in children with influenza: a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, positive parallel-controlled study.
abstract:
CONTEXT: High-quality evidence on Lianhua Qingwen (LHQW) for treating influenza in children remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of LHQW in children aged 3-14 years with influenza, compared with oseltamivir.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, positive parallel-controlled trial, participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either LHQW + oseltamivir placebo or oseltamivir + LHQW placebo. The primary outcome was clinical recovery time. Secondary outcomes included time to defervescence, symptom scores on the Canadian Acute Respiratory Illness and Flu Scale, the incidence of complications and severe/critical influenza, and the improvement rates for individual influenza symptoms. Safety outcomes were assessed based on adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 520 participants were randomized (260 per group). Baseline characteristics were comparable. Median clinical recovery time was 5 days in both groups, with similar clinical recovery rates (71.5% vs. 71.2%; HR: 1.04, 95% CI: 0.84-1.29; one-sided p < 0.025). Median time to defervescence was shorter with LHQW (24 h vs. 30 h, p < 0.05). LHQW showed higher improvement rates for cough (56.9% vs. 45.5%) and sore throat (90.9% vs. 74.2%) (both p < 0.05). No severe or critical influenza occurred in the LHQW group. Adverse events incidence was similar between groups (p > 0.05).
DISCUSSION: LHQW may offer a safe and effective alternative to oseltamivir for pediatric influenza, with particular benefits for defervescence, cough, and sore throat.
CONCLUSIONS: LHQW was non-inferior to oseltamivir in clinical recovery time and resulted in faster defervescence and greater improvement in cough and sore throat, with comparable safety.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR1900028390 (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, Dec. 20, 2019).

title: Prehospital Analgesia in Trauma: A Systematic Review of Current Evidence.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pain management is integral to prehospital trauma care. However, due to multiple challenges, pain is frequently undertreated despite important physiologic and psychologic implications. Among these challenges is uncertainty regarding the safety and effectiveness of pharmacologic agents administered enroute. We aimed to evaluate the level of evidence for the safety and effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adult trauma patients.
METHODS: An electronic database search of PUBMED, Google Scholar, Cochrane Library, Embase and Scopus for studies that reported on safety and/or effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adults (aged > 15 years) from January 1st, 2014, to January 1st, 2026. Non-original studies, paediatric studies, studies of non-pharmacologic agents or non-systemic administration (e.g., topical) were excluded.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies, involving 17,115 patients, met the inclusion criteria. The studies consisted of 6 randomized controlled trials, 5 retrospective cohort studies, one retrospective comparative study, one retrospective observational study, two prospective observational studies, one prospective cohort study and one non-randomized clinical trial. Agents included opioids, ketamine, methoxyflurane and paracetamol. Apart from one study of opioid therapy, no drug-attributed serious adverse events were reported. Minor adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness, dysphoria, agitation and drowsiness were common. All agents demonstrated effectiveness to varying levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence demonstrates an overall favourable safety and effectiveness profile of prehospital analgesia for adult trauma patients. However, considering the wide prehospital prevalence of injury-related pain, evidence is limited by scope, methodology and variations of treatment protocols.

title: Long-term safety profile of opicapone in patients with Parkinson's disease and early fluctuations.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motor fluctuations frequently emerge within the first few years of levodopa treatment in Parkinson's disease (PD), increasing symptom burden and treatment complexity. While opicapone is an established adjunct therapy for motor fluctuations, its safety profile when initiated early in the course of fluctuating disease remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: This pooled post-hoc analysis integrated individual patient-level data from two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of opicapone 50 mg and their open-label extensions. Analyses focused on patients with recent onset of motor fluctuations (≤2 years). Safety outcomes included the incidence, severity, timing, and evolution of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) during double-blind and up to 1 year of open-label exposure, with comparisons between earlier (OPC-OPC) and delayed (PLC-OPC) initiation.
RESULTS: A total of 269 patients with recent motor fluctuations were included, of whom 228 entered open-label treatment. During the double-blind phase, TEAEs were reported in 55.9% of patients receiving opicapone and 50.9% receiving placebo, with no statistically significant difference between groups. Adverse events were mainly mild to moderate and occurred predominantly within the first 2-3 weeks declining thereafter. Dyskinesia was the most frequent TEAE (10.2% vs. 3.6%, p = 0.09), occurring early and resolving in most patients, either spontaneously or following modest levodopa dose adjustment. Across the combined study period, overall TEAE incidence and cumulative dyskinesia rates were comparable between early and delayed initiation groups (15.3% vs. 15.5%, p = 1.0), with no increase over time.
CONCLUSION: Opicapone demonstrated a favorable and consistent safety profile in patients with recent onset of motor fluctuations, with adverse events predominantly transient and manageable. Earlier initiation was not associated with an increased safety burden and showed numerically lower rates of overall TEAEs and dyskinesia compared with broader trial populations. These findings support the hypothesis that early optimization of levodopa therapy with opicapone does not accelerate the development of motor complications, supporting early COMT-inhibition in fluctuating PD.

title: Investigating the Effect of Oral Probiotic Capsules on Postpartum Sleep Quality in Primiparous Women: A triple-blind randomised controlled trial.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Quality of sleep is an important indicator of health. Sleep disturbance and daytime fatigue is one of the most common problems in the postpartum period. Early postpartum (first 4 weeks) is when sleep is most disturbed. The gut microbiota may affect sleep quality and affect host health through the production of metabolites and compounds. This study aimed to determine the effect of oral probiotic capsule on the quality of sleep after delivery in primiparous women.
METHOD: This triple-blind randomised controlled trial study was conducted in August to November 2023 with eligible primiparous women who gave birth at Health Centers No. 2 and 3, Mashhad, Iran. The participants were randomly and equally divided into two groups: (1) the probiotic group, which received probiotic capsules (containing Lactobacillus acidophilus, Bifidobacterium bifidum, B. lactis and B. longum) and (2) the placebo group, which received placebo capsules. All participants received one capsule daily from the third day after delivery for 30 days. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire was completed before and after the study. Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests, T-test and Mann-Whitney test were used for statistical analysis. A P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 60 women were included in this study (n = 30 for each group). The two groups were homogeneous in terms of demographic and obstetric characteristics except for body mass index. Before the intervention, the overall score of postpartum quality of sleep in the probiotic and placebo groups was 9.66 ± 6.21 and 11.70 ± 6.68, respectively; after the intervention, the probiotic group had a score of 6.16 ± 2.75 with the score difference of -3.50 ± 5.53 and the placebo group a score of 6.60 ± 2.66 with the score difference of -5.10 ± 6.31 with a statistically significant difference in the intervention group compared to the placebo (P = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: Consumption of probiotic capsules improves the quality of sleep and maternal health in the postpartum period.

title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test the efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid versus sham injection for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
DESIGN: Single centred, participant and assessor masked, three arm randomised controlled trial (Inject trial).
SETTING: Community.
PARTICIPANTS: From 5 December 2019 and 24 July 2022, 192 adults (18 years or older) diagnosed with midportion Achilles tendinopathy were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63), or high volume injection with corticosteroid (n=65).
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were allocated to sham injection (2-3 mL 0.5% bupivacaine hydrochloride), high volume injection with corticosteroid (50 mL saline and 0.5% bupivacaine with 25 mg hydrocortisone in the first 10 mL), or high volume injection with no corticosteroid (same solution but without hydrocortisone). They received the same exercise programme, education, and activity modification advice.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was pain and disability using the validated VISA-A and the primary endpoint was at 52 weeks. The economic outcome was cost per quality-adjusted life-years from a societal perspective.
RESULTS: VISA-A data were obtained from 181 (94%) of 192 participants at 12 months. No clear differences were noted between sham and high volume injection either with (-3.5 (98.33% confidence interval -12.0 to 5.0)) or without corticosteroid (4.0 (-4.2 to 12.3)), and between the two injections (-7.5 (-15.3 to 0.3)), at 12 months. The point estimate was closest to the target difference for the comparison between injections and favoured the arm without steroid. The only differences observed on VISA-A at intermediate time points were a benefit for high volume with corticosteroid versus sham at six weeks (9.2 (1.5 to 16.9)) but worse outcomes for high volume injection with corticosteroid versus high volume injection with no corticosteroid at 26 weeks (-8.6 (-16.4 to -0.7)). The health economic analysis found high volume injection with corticosteroid to be less costly than the sham with similar effectiveness based on quality-adjusted life-years (>0.90 probability of being cost effective at $AUD50 000 and $100 000 willingness-to-pay thresholds). No serious trial related adverse events were recorded.
CONCLUSION: High volume injections with or without corticosteroids did not improve pain or disability compared with sham at 12 months. Although high volume injections with corticosteroid showed short term clinical benefit and potential reduction in healthcare costs over a year, they were associated with worse longer term clinical outcomes. The clinical data do not support routine use for high volume injections with corticosteroid for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12619001455156.

title: Phase 1 Study of Safety and PK With A Combination of Omeprazole and Trimetazidine for Fatty Acid Oxidation Inhibition in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors.
abstract: Fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a metabolic vulnerability in cancer cells, making pharmacologic FAO inhibition a promising therapeutic strategy. This Phase I, open-label, 3 + 3 dose-escalation study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of two oral FAO inhibitors-omeprazole (KN510), a carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase inhibitor, and trimetazidine (KN713), an acetyl-CoA acyltransferase inhibitor-given once daily in combination to patients with advanced solid tumors. Twelve patients were enrolled across four dose cohorts (omeprazole and trimetazidine, each 60-120 mg/day). The maximum tolerated dose was not reached; the recommended Phase 2 dose was set at 120 mg once daily for each agent. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with most adverse events Grade 1-2; the most common were flu-like symptoms (25.0%), constipation (16.7%), nausea (16.7%), and dizziness (16.7%). Omeprazole showed time-dependent pharmacokinetics consistent with auto-inhibition of its own metabolism, whereas trimetazidine showed dose-proportional pharmacokinetics across the studied range. The best response was stable disease in five patients (disease control rate 41.7%). Median progression-free survival was 1.66 months (95% CI, 1.18-3.55) and median overall survival was 9.13 months (95% CI, 3.29-not reached). Dual pharmacologic FAO inhibition with oral omeprazole and trimetazidine was feasible and well tolerated, supporting the mechanistic rationale for combination dosing. Disease stabilization observed in this heavily pretreated population warrants further clinical evaluation, particularly in combination with standard chemotherapy regimens. title: Anaprazole-based versus rabeprazole-based quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori eradication: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the efficacy and safety of a bismuth-containing quadruple therapy comprising the novel proton pump inhibitor (PPI) anaprazole versus the classical PPI rabeprazole, both combined with amoxicillin and furazolidone, for Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication.
METHODS: A prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label, non-inferiority design was employed. Consecutive treatment-naïve patients positive for H. pylori who visited the gastroenterology departments of four hospitals in Jiangsu Province between August 2025 and February 2026 were enrolled. Eligible patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to two groups: the anaprazole group (anaprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin 1000 mg, furazolidone 100 mg, and colloidal bismuth pectin 300 mg, twice daily) and the rabeprazole group (rabeprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin 1000 mg, furazolidone 100 mg, and colloidal bismuth pectin 300 mg, twice daily). Both groups received a 14-day treatment course. H. pylori eradication was assessed by ¹³C-urea breath test at 4 weeks after the completion of therapy.
RESULTS: A total of 320 patients were enrolled, with 160 in each group. In the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis, the eradication rate was 81.9% (95% CI: 75.2% to 87.1%) in the anaprazole group and 80.0% (95% CI: 73.1% to 85.5%) in the rabeprazole group, with a difference of 1.9% (95% CI: -6.7% to 10.5%, P=0.67). In the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis, the eradication rates were 89.1% (95% CI: 83.1% to 93.2%) and 88.9% (95% CI: 82.7% to 93.1%), respectively (difference: 0.2%; 95% CI: -7.0% to 7.4%, P=0.95). In the per-protocol (PP) analysis, the eradication rates were 90.9% (95% CI: 85.2% to 94.6%) and 90.0% (95% CI: 83.9% to 94.0%), respectively (difference: 0.9%; 95% CI: -5.8% to 7.6%, P=0.80). Regarding safety, the incidence of adverse events was slightly higher in the anaprazole group compared to the rabeprazole group (22.50% vs. 15.00%), but the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.09). Medication adherence was similar between the two groups (P=0.60).
CONCLUSION: The quadruple regimen consisting of anaprazole combined with amoxicillin, furazolidone, and bismuth is non-inferior to the rabeprazole-based quadruple regimen for the eradication of H. pylori infection. There were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of eradication rate, incidence of adverse reactions, or medication adherence. Anaprazole, as an acid-suppressive agent, achieves satisfactory efficacy in H. pylori eradication therapy and holds promise for clinical application.

title: Persistent monocyte activation and remodeling in people with HIV after 36 months of switching from a 3-drug regimen to B/F/TAF or DTG/3TC: a sub-study of the DEBATE trial.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The DEBATE study is a randomised trial comparing standard three-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) with either a two-drug regimen (DTG/3TC) or an alternative three-drug regimen (B/F/TAF) in people with HIV who are virally suppressed. While these regimens are effective in controlling the virus, their impact on the innate immune system is less well understood. Monocytes play a pivotal role in inflammation by bridging innate and adaptive immunity and maintaining the viral reservoir. Persistent monocyte activation in individuals treated with ART, as indicated by altered subsets, proinflammatory cytokines and soluble markers, has been associated with chronic inflammation and non-AIDS comorbidities. This highlights the clinical relevance of monocyte activation even when viral suppression is achieved.
METHODS: Eleven virally suppressed people with HIV (PWH) randomized to switch to dolutegravir/lamivudine (DTG/3TC, n=6) or to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF, n=5) were studied. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) collected at baseline and 36 months after the switch were analyzed using a 17-parameter flow cytometry panel to characterize monocyte phenotype.
RESULTS: Monocyte remodeling in chronically infected, ART-treated PWH involved chemokine receptors such as CX3CR1, CCR5 and CXCR4, which play important roles in cell migration, inflammation and viral reservoir maintenance. Moreover, the upregulation of TAM receptors (MerTK and Tyro3) and CD38 might enhance inflammatory effects in people switching to another three-drug regimen (3DR, B/F/TAF) rather than in those switching to a two-drug regimen (2DR, DTG/3TC). Nonetheless, in DTG/3TC-treated people, inflammation and viral reservoir maintenance might be promoted by the pSTAT3 pathway.
DISCUSSION: Persistent monocyte activation and immune senescence remain detectable in ART-experienced, virologically suppressed people with HIV after switching to either B/F/TAF or DTG/3TC, indicating that regimen optimization alone does not restore innate immune homeostasis. The enhanced expression of migratory and HIV-related receptors suggests ongoing reservoir maintenance and residual inflammation.

title: Quadratus Lumborum versus Transversus Abdominis Plane Block with Oxycodone or Sufentanil for Recovery Quality After Laparoscopic Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery: A Factorial Randomized Trial.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Quadratus lumborum block (QLB) theoretically provides broader visceral analgesia than transversus abdominis plane block (TAPB), while oxycodone, a dual μ- and κ-opioid receptor agonist, may offer superior visceral pain control compared with sufentanil. We evaluated these two regional techniques and two opioid regimens simultaneously in a factorial design to determine their effects on recovery after laparoscopic gastrointestinal cancer surgery.
METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, 2×2 factorial trial, 120 adults were randomly assigned to bilateral QLB or TAPB (0.375% ropivacaine 20 mL per side) and oxycodone or sufentanil patient-controlled analgesia. All patients received intraoperative dexmedetomidine and flurbiprofen axetil. The primary outcome was 24-h recovery quality (15-item quality of recovery scale; minimal clinically important difference 6 points). Secondary outcomes included recovery quality at 48 and 72 h, visceral and incisional pain, opioid consumption, rescue analgesia, and adverse events.
RESULTS: For 24-h recovery quality, no significant interaction was found between block and opioid (P = 0.283); QLB vs TAPB (mean [SD] 102.1 [7.9] vs 102.6 [7.6]; mean difference -0.5, 95% CI -3.3 to 2.4; P = 0.740) and oxycodone vs sufentanil (103.7 [6.9] vs 100.9 [8.3]; mean difference 2.8, 95% CI 0.1 to 5.6; P = 0.045) did not reach the Bonferroni-corrected threshold (P < 0.025) or the 6-point difference. Oxycodone was associated with lower visceral pain scores at 1, 6, 24 and 48 h, lower incisional pain scores at 1 and 6 h, and decreased rescue analgesia use (13.3% vs 29.3%). Other outcomes were comparable.
CONCLUSION: Within comprehensive multimodal analgesia, neither QLB nor oxycodone demonstrated superior recovery compared with TAPB or sufentanil. Exploratory findings of lower postoperative pain and less rescue analgesia with oxycodone should be considered hypothesis-generating.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400080766).

title: Levodopa or dopamine agonists for enhancing motor function after stroke.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
abstract:
RATIONALE: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. There is a lack of evidence regarding pharmacological enhancement of stroke recovery with dopamine agonists or levodopa, in particular in terms of motor deficits.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of dopaminergic agents, defined as levodopa or dopamine agonists, on improving motor function after stroke.
SEARCH METHODS: We conducted an extensive database search on the Cochrane Stroke Group trials register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Science Citation Index Expanded, CPCI-S, BIOSIS Citation Index, ProQuest Dissertation and Theses Global up to November 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that enrolled participants with a clinical diagnosis of stroke, irrespective of age or stroke aetiology and without a pre-existing indication for the use of levodopa or dopamine agonists. Eligible trials compared levodopa or dopamine agonists with a comparator group who received placebo or no medication, with equivalent rehabilitative care in both groups, and aimed at enhancing motor function after stroke.
OUTCOMES: Motor function was the critical benefit outcome. As a critical harm outcome, we assessed serious adverse events. Important outcomes consisted of death, recurrent stroke, disability, dependence, health-related quality of life, activities of daily living, total number of adverse events, and psychiatric adverse events.
RISK OF BIAS: Two review authors independently assessed the risk of bias for each trial using the Cochrane Risk of bias tool (RoB 1).
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesised results for each outcome using a standardised mean difference (SMD) or mean difference (MD) for continuous data and risk ratio (RR) for dichotomous results, with a random-effects model due to heterogeneity between the trials. For non-extractable trials due to missing numerical data, we synthesised the results narratively. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 12 parallel-group RCTs involving 1860 participants. The trials were conducted in Europe, the USA and Asia, and were published between 2001 and 2025. All trials included participants with either ischaemic strokes only or both haemorrhagic and ischaemic strokes. The mean age of all included participants ranged from 55 to 78 years. Of the included trials, 10 were placebo-controlled and two compared levodopa or dopamine agonists against usual care. Eleven trials investigated levodopa as the intervention and one examined the dopamine agonist ropinirole.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Across 12 included trials, complete data on motor function were available for six trials with continuous data (1258 participants) and for two trials with dichotomous data (615 participants), of which one trial assessed both continuous and dichotomous data. We detected no difference in motor function scores between levodopa or dopamine agonists and the comparator groups for continuous outcomes (SMD 1.42, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.20 to 3.05; 6 trials, 1258 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The wide confidence intervals indicate substantial imprecision in the effect estimate. Consistent with those results, we detected no difference for dichotomous motor function outcomes either (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.82 to 1.06; 2 trials, 615 participants; anticipated absolute event rate of having a favourable outcome of 581/1000 in the comparator group versus 540/1000 with levodopa/dopamine agonists; low-certainty evidence). Heterogeneity for the critical outcome motor function (continuously measured) was high (I2 = 99%). However, a sensitivity analysis including only two trials with a low risk of bias in all domains, that accounted for the majority of the included patient population (1025 of 1258), showed no heterogeneity (I2 = 0%), and a smaller confidence interval (SMD 0.02, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.14; 2 trials, 1025 participants), implying no difference between groups. Six trials assessed serious adverse events, including 1281 participants. There was no notable difference in the risk of serious adverse events between groups (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.83 to 1.27; anticipated absolute event rate of 302/1000 events in comparators versus 311/1000 events with levodopa/dopamine agonists; low-certainty evidence). All important outcomes showed no notable between-group differences. The certainty of evidence, according to GRADE, was very low for continuously measured scores of motor function, low for dichotomous motor function outcomes, and low for serious adverse events. Together with heterogeneity in both interventions and outcomes, inconsistency of findings, imprecision related to small sample sizes in some trials, and imprecision of summary effect, there are major limitations of the current evidence.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Based on limited data, we did not find evidence that the use of levodopa or dopamine agonists improves motor function after a stroke. Given the low certainty of evidence due to limited data, wide confidence intervals, and heterogeneity across trials, further research may change this assessment and explore whether effects are different in specific subgroups of patients.
FUNDING: Science funds [Wissenschaftsfonds] Department of Rehabilitation and Neurology, University Department of Geriatric Medicine, Felix Platter, University of Basel, Switzerland. This review had no external funding.
REGISTRATION: Protocol available via https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013416.

title: Timing of intratracheal administration of budesonide mixed with surfactant to prevent bronchopulmonary dysplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: The aim of this study was to evaluate whether intratracheal budesonide mixed with surfactant prevents bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and whether timing contributes to heterogeneity. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and trial registries for randomised controlled trials of budesonide-surfactant versus surfactant alone. Random-effects meta-analyses yielded risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We assessed risk of bias with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. A post hoc subgroup analysis classified trials by whether treatment was restricted to within 4 h after birth or permitted after 4 h. We included 15 trials (3522 infants); 14 trials (3494 infants) reported BPD at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (BPD36). The overall analysis suggested a reduction in BPD36 (RR 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59-0.86; I2 = 68%), although heterogeneity was substantial. BPD36 was reduced in trials restricting treatment to within 4 h (RR 0.58; 95% CI, 0.46-0.72; eight trials; 1065 infants), but not in trials permitting later treatment (RR 0.98; 95% CI, 0.91-1.06; four trials; 2011 infants; P for subgroup difference < 0.00001). The composite outcome of BPD or death showed a similar pattern. Mortality and most other neonatal outcomes did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSION: In trials restricting treatment to within 4 h after birth, budesonide-surfactant therapy may reduce BPD36; however, this post hoc, trial-level finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect differences between earlier small and contemporary large trials. Current evidence does not support routine budesonide-surfactant therapy. A large prospective trial of early administration is needed to determine whether timing modifies benefit.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD42024547670).
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Earlier small trials suggested that budesonide mixed with surfactant reduces BPD, whereas recent large multicentre trials found little or no benefit. • The source of the marked heterogeneity among trials remains uncertain.
WHAT IS NEW: • Trials restricting treatment to within 4 h showed reductions in BPD36 and BPD or death, whereas trials permitting later treatment showed no benefit. • This post hoc association with timing may reflect study-level confounding and small-study effects and requires confirmation.

title: The Effect of Bupropion in Peripheral Neuropathic Pain A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoamine reuptake inhibitors are evidenced first-line treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. The aim was to investigate if bupropion, a drug that specifically inhibits neuronal noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake, relieves neuropathic pain and if a potential effect depends on status of conditioned pain modulation (CPM) and sensory phenotype (irritable vs. non-irritable nociceptor).
METHOD: Study design was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and cross-over. Patients with peripheral neuropathic pain were treated with bupropion and placebo in a random order, with treatment periods lasting 6 weeks preceded by a 1-week baseline. Change in daily average pain was the primary outcome. Other outcomes included pain relief and 30% and 50% pain reduction.
RESULTS: 67 patients were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean daily average pain changed from NRS 6.4 to 5.5 after bupropion treatment with an average effect as compared with placebo of -0.5 (95% CI -0.8 to -0.1, p = 0.005). No relation was found between response to treatment and efficiency of CPM or sensory phenotype. There was no significant effect on the pain relief scale. A 30% and 50% pain reduction was found in 10 and 6 patients respectively with a NNT for 50% pain reduction of 15. Bupropion was well tolerated.
CONCLUSION: Bupropion had a pain-relieving effect independent of CPM efficiency and sensory phenotype. NNT for 50% pain reduction was higher than reported for first-line treatments, but bupropion treatment may still be an option in patients with insufficient response or intolerable side effects on such treatments.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study finds a modest pain-relieving effect of bupropion on peripheral neuropathic pain independent of function of conditioned pain modulation. Bupropion could be an alternative treatment for patients with a lack of effect or intolerable side effects to first-choice treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. Further, larger studies are needed to determine optimal dosage.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered with the EU clinical trials Register (EudraCT 2019-000243-27) on March 15th 2019. The study is approved by the Ethical Committee of the Region of Southern Denmark (also included approval for Regions of Central Denmark; no. S-20190010) and the Danish Medicine Agency (no. 2019012986) and is registered with the Danish Data Protection Agency (via the Region of Southern Denmark's internal notification; no. 19/17111).

title: Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA.
RESULTS: A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ.
CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

title: A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, positive-controlled study of the general treatment method using Tanreqing capsule in uncomplicated influenza.
journal: Journal of traditional Chinese medicine = Chung i tsa chih ying wen pan
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of the method of clearing heat, resolving phlegm, and detoxification, represented by Tanreqing capsule (TRQC, ), on influenza.
METHODS: A total of 122 patients with uncomplicated influenza in the Beijing-Tianjin area were randomly divided into an observation group and a control group. They were treated with TRQC plus oseltamivir placebo or oseltamivir plus TRQC placebo for 5 d, respectively. The relief time for influenza symptoms, individual symptom relief time, the frequency of antipyretic drug usage, and the frequency of antibiotic drug usage were analyzed.
RESULTS: External wind-cold syndrome (28.69%) and external wind-heat syndrome (45.08%) were the most common syndrome types. The number of patients in TRQC group achieved normal temperature within 1 d was significantly more than oseltamivir group (72.88% vs50.80%, P < 0.05). There were no significant differences in the time for influenza symptom relief and individual symptom relief between the two groups. TRQC showed a better heat relief effect than oseltamivir on the fifth day of treatment.
CONCLUSION: TRQC, as a "Tongzhi" method (General treatment), has a curative effect on uncomplicated influenza that is similar to oseltamivir, with a better effect on prolonged fever. TRQC is an effective method of general treatment for influenza and can serve as an alternative therapy for managing large-scale influenza epidemics.
